map.area: Miller current julie-server INVOCATION + process layer
map.summary: Miller drives julie-server entirely through one synchronous subprocess wrapper, JulieExtractRunner (src/Miller.Indexing/JulieExtractRunner.cs). It launches the pinned binary `.tools/julie-server[.exe]` resolved under WorkspaceContext.ToolsRoot (= AppContext.BaseDirectory/.tools), falling back to PATH, and always invokes the single `extract` subcommand with one of four operations: `scan`, `info`, `update`, `delete`. argv is built via ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList (no shell), stdout/stderr are captured asynchronously, the process runs with UseShellExecute=false and CreateNoWindow=true, and the exit code is mapped 0→parsed ExtractReport, 1→JulieExtractFailedException, 2→JulieExtractUsageException, else→JulieExtractException. On exit 0 it additionally cross-checks schema(28)/extract_contract_version(3)/hash_algorithm(blake3) against MillerExtractContract and throws IncompatibleExtractException on mismatch. Both a full whole-repo scan (force or delta) and per-file update/delete incremental paths exist; the incremental path is driven by a leader-elected FileSystemWatcher in IndexerService/IndexerCore. Notably there is NO timeout, NO CancellationToken, NO Kill, NO WorkingDirectory, and NO env-var manipulation on the spawn — it is a bare WaitForExit().

key_files.role: The subprocess wrapper. Static argv builders (BuildScanArgs/BuildInfoArgs/BuildUpdateArgs/BuildDeleteArgs), exit-code mapper Interpret(), report parser ParseReport(), binary resolver Locate(), and the live Run() that spawns the process.
The typed exception hierarchy: JulieExtractException (base, carries StandardError), JulieExtractFailedException (exit 1, carries parsed Errors), JulieExtractUsageException (exit 2, stderr-only).
The JSON report record (snake_case) parsed from julie stdout, plus ExtractError record. Includes M3 freshness fields workspace_id/revision/files_updated/files_deleted/hash_algorithm.
Pinned-version constants the post-extract cross-check gates on: schema 28, contract 3, hash blake3, julie-server 7.13.2.
VerifyReport() — the post-exit-0 schema/contract/hash cross-check that throws IncompatibleExtractException; called at the end of Run().
FromCanonicalRoot() = SHA-256 hex of the canonical root; supplies the --workspace-id arg on scan.
realpath-style symlink-resolving canonicalizer for root and --file args (verified-fact 4); used by JulieExtractOps before each call.
Interface abstracting Update(path)/Delete(path)/Scan(force) so IndexerCore is testable without spawning julie.
Production IExtractOps: canonicalizes root once at construction, per-file path on each call, then delegates to runner.Update/Delete/Scan.
Startup: locates the binary, decides the first scan (missing DB → delta scan; mismatched workspace_id → force scan; matching → reuse), runs runner.Scan() with the canonical db path.

Leader-elected FileSystemWatcher host; on ~1s debounce drains coalesced events into update/delete/scan, runs a startup delta scan, and exposes TryReindexAsLeader (update) / TryScanAsLeader (scan/force).
Pure dispatch core: routes a drained batch to UpdateOp/DeleteOp/ScanOp, executes one-in-flight, isolates per-op failures (transient codes data_loss_guard/flock_timeout at INFO, else ERROR).
Defines ToolsRoot = AppContext.BaseDirectory/.tools and ExtractDbPath = <root>/.miller/symbols.db.

facts.claim: stdout and stderr are drained asynchronously (BeginOutputReadLine/BeginErrorReadLine into StringBuilders) to avoid pipe-buffer deadlock, then trimmed of trailing newlines.

facts.claim: There is NO timeout, NO CancellationToken, and NO Kill on the spawn — it blocks indefinitely on a bare WaitForExit().
facts.evidence: JulieExtractRunner.cs:314 `process.WaitForExit();` (no timeout overload). grep of the file for WorkingDirectory|EnvironmentVariables|CancellationToken|Kill returned only the WaitForExit() line; the Run() signature takes only IReadOnlyList<string> args (:274) — no token parameter.

facts.claim: No WorkingDirectory is set, so the child inherits the Miller process CWD; no environment variables are added or modified.
facts.evidence: ProcessStartInfo at JulieExtractRunner.cs:276-283 sets only FileName, RedirectStandardOutput, RedirectStandardError, UseShellExecute, CreateNoWindow — no WorkingDirectory and no psi.Environment/EnvironmentVariables access anywhere in the file (grep returned no matches).

facts.claim: Exit-code contract: 0→parsed report; 1→JulieExtractFailedException (parses errors from the still-emitted failed report on stdout, falls back to empty list + stderr); 2→JulieExtractUsageException (stderr only, stdout NOT parsed); any other→JulieExtractException.
facts.evidence: JulieExtractRunner.cs:167-198 switch on exitCode: case 0 `return ParseReport(stdout)`; case 1 parses `ParseReport(stdout).Errors` in try/catch(JsonException)→Array.Empty, then `throw new JulieExtractFailedException(...errors, stderr)`; case 2 `throw new JulieExtractUsageException(stderr)`; default `throw new JulieExtractException($"...unexpected code {exitCode}.", stderr)`.

facts.claim: A failed exec (wrong-arch/non-executable/permission) surfaces as Win32Exception and is wrapped into JulieExtractException, not silently swallowed.
facts.evidence: JulieExtractRunner.cs:300-309 catch(System.ComponentModel.Win32Exception ex) → `throw new JulieExtractException($"Failed to exec julie-server ...corrupt/wrong-arch/non-executable binary?...", standardError: string.Empty, ex);`

facts.claim: After exit 0 it does a Miller-side version cross-check because julie only self-rejects a NEWER DB; an older/drifted schema(28)/contract(3)/hash(blake3) throws IncompatibleExtractException.
facts.evidence: JulieExtractRunner.cs:322 `ExtractVersionMismatch.VerifyReport(report);` after Interpret; ExtractVersionMismatch.cs:55-85 compares report.SchemaVersion!=28, ExtractContractVersion!=3, and HashAlgorithm!=blake3, throwing IncompatibleExtractException; MillerExtractContract.cs:13-15 constants 28/3/blake3.

facts.claim: The incremental path is driven by a leader-elected FileSystemWatcher: events are coalesced and drained on a ~1s debounce into update/delete/scan, one subprocess in-flight.
facts.evidence: IndexerService.cs:28 `DebounceInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1)`; :196-197 `lock (_opsGate) _core.DrainAndProcess(headChanged);`; IndexerCore.cs:127-133 routes ops to `_ops.Update/_ops.Delete/_ops.Scan`; :89 'The whole drain+execute runs under one lock so a second debounce tick cannot interleave a concurrent subprocess'.

facts.claim: update is safe to call on any change (julie blake3-no-ops unchanged content); delete is idempotent (status=not_found, exit 0).
facts.evidence: JulieExtractRunner.cs:231-232 doc 'julie blake3-checks the content and no-ops (status=unchanged, no revision bump) if it is identical'; :250-251 doc 'Idempotent: a second delete reports status=not_found (exit 0), not a failure.'

facts.claim: update/delete require ALL THREE paths (db, root, file) already canonical (absolute + symlink-resolved); the runner does NOT GetFullPath-mangle them, and RequireCanonicalDb rejects a non-rooted db.

facts.claim: IndexerCore treats data_loss_guard and flock_timeout as transient (logged INFO, prior index kept); all other exit-1 codes or unparseable failures are ERROR/WARNING but never abort the batch.
facts.evidence: IndexerCore.cs:119-120 `TransientErrorCodes = { "data_loss_guard", "flock_timeout" }`; :152-167 transient→LogInformation else→LogError; :169-192 catch(Exception)→LogWarning; all branches keep the prior index and continue.

contract_points: Binary name: 'julie-server' on Unix, 'julie-server.exe' on Windows (JulieExtractRunner.cs:61). Consumers must ship exactly this filename under .tools/.
Resolution order: <ToolsRoot>/julie-server[.exe] (= AppContext.BaseDirectory/.tools) first, then each PATH entry. Repo cwd is NOT searched.
Single subcommand 'extract' with operation tokens scan|info|update|delete, always preceded by '--json'.
scan argv (exact, in order): extract --db <ABS_DB> --root <ABS_ROOT> --workspace-id <SHA256_HEX_ID> --json scan [--force].
info argv: extract --db <ABS_DB> --json info  (no --root, no flock, read-only-safe under a live writer).
update argv: extract --db <ABS_DB> --root <ABS_ROOT> --json update --file <ABS_FILE>.
delete argv: extract --db <ABS_DB> --root <ABS_ROOT> --json delete --file <ABS_FILE>.
--workspace-id value = lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical (symlink-resolved) root (WorkspaceId.FromCanonicalRoot).

Exit-code contract julie must honor: 0 = success with a JSON ExtractReport on stdout; 1 = operation failure WITH a failed ExtractReport (status/errors) still on stdout; 2 = usage/argv error with clap text on stderr and NO stdout JSON; anything else is treated as a crash.

Output is a single JSON object on stdout, snake_case keys, parsed into ExtractReport. serde renames Rust field `db`→`db_path`. Counts are unsigned (ulong). Freshness fields workspace_id/revision/files_updated/files_deleted/hash_algorithm are part of the report.

Report must carry schema_version=28, extract_contract_version=3, hash_algorithm='blake3' or Miller rejects it with IncompatibleExtractException (MillerExtractContract). hash_algorithm MUST be present and exactly 'blake3' (ordinal).
julie must NOT mkdir the DB parent dir for scan — Miller creates it (JulieExtractRunner.Scan ensures it). The .db file itself may be absent on first scan.

Paths passed to update/delete (db, root, file) are already canonical/symlink-resolved and absolute; Miller passes them verbatim. julie's inside-root validation must accept them as-is (verified-fact 4).
No timeout / cancellation: julie-server is expected to terminate on its own. Miller WaitForExit()s indefinitely with no kill — a hung julie-server hangs the calling Miller thread.
No special environment is supplied; julie-server inherits Miller's environment and current working directory (no WorkingDirectory set on the child).
risks: No timeout and no CancellationToken on the spawn (JulieExtractRunner.cs:314 bare WaitForExit()): a hung or wedged julie-server blocks the bootstrap StartAsync (synchronous, before the MCP transport starts) or the indexer debounce/Try* call indefinitely with no escape and no Kill.

No WorkingDirectory is set, so a relative --db/--root would resolve against Miller's ambient CWD inside julie. Miller mitigates by always passing absolute/canonical paths, but anything that ever passes a relative path would silently target the wrong tree.

Exit-1 stdout parsing is best-effort: if julie ever changes to NOT emit a failed report on stdout for exit 1, errors degrade to an empty list and only stderr survives (JulieExtractRunner.cs:175-189) — the failure is still surfaced but loses its structured codes (e.g. transient classification in IndexerCore would misroute to ERROR).

Version cross-check only fires when the report INCLUDES schema/contract fields; null versions are NOT cross-checked at the extract boundary (ExtractVersionMismatch.VerifyReport deliberately skips null, relying on the read-path gate). A report omitting them but with a stale DB would pass the extract gate.

hash_algorithm presence is enforced at the extract boundary, so a julie build/operation that omits hash_algorithm in the report (even if otherwise valid) fails every scan/update/delete with IncompatibleExtractException — tightly coupled to julie always emitting that field.
open_questions: Whether julie-server ever legitimately exits with a code other than 0/1/2 under normal operation (e.g. a signal/panic exit) — Miller maps all such to JulieExtractException as a crash, which is correct only if julie's contract truly reserves 0/1/2.

The exact set of julie error `code` strings beyond data_loss_guard and flock_timeout (which IndexerCore hardcodes as transient) — confirm against julie's report.rs error taxonomy that no other code should be treated as transient/retryable.

Whether julie emits the JSON report as a single line or pretty-printed/multi-line on stdout — Miller appends lines and parses the whole accumulated buffer (JulieExtractRunner.cs:291,317), which works for either, but the assumption that the entire stdout is exactly one JSON object (no log noise on stdout) is unverified against julie's actual stdout behavior.

map.area: Miller SQLite schema DEPENDENCY — every table/column/query Miller reads from the julie-server extract DB
map.summary: Miller reads 11 julie-owned tables from the `julie-server extract` SQLite DB across 6 reader classes in src/Miller.Indexing (plus zero in Miller.Core, which is pure I/O-free logic). It builds its OWN in-memory BM25 inverted index (Miller.Core.Search.MillerSearchIndex) from raw `symbols` rows — it does NOT read any FTS5/MATCH/porter/bm25() table; grep across all of src found zero FTS SQL. The compatibility contract is enforced by JulieSchemaGate.Verify before bulk reads: it requires `schema_version` (schema=28), `external_extract_metadata` (keys extract_contract_version=3 and hash_algorithm='blake3'). File freshness uses `files.hash` (raw-byte BLAKE3) guarded by `external_extract_metadata.hash_algorithm='blake3'`. Miller reads `symbols.metadata` JSON for exactly two keys: `is_test` (bool) and `test_role` (string). Miller CREATEs only two of its own tables (`workspaces` in ~/.miller/workspaces.db, `tool_telemetry` in its telemetry DB) — these are not part of julie's extract and are not in this dependency surface.

key_files.role: Compatibility gate run on the open read-only connection before bulk reads; defines the REQUIRED tables/keys contract (schema_version, external_extract_metadata)
Single source of truth for pinned versions: ExpectedSchemaVersion=28, ExpectedExtractContractVersion=3, ExpectedHashAlgorithm=blake3, PinnedJulieServerVersion=7.13.2
Bulk startup reader: SELECTs symbols rows; parses symbols.metadata JSON for is_test/test_role
Cross-language bridge reader: SELECTs type_arguments, literals, symbol_annotations, and DbSet<T> property rows from symbols
Edge reader: SELECTs relationships and identifiers to build the dependency graph

On-demand inspect/edit reader: SELECTs symbol detail/edit-span columns from symbols, references/callees/rename-sites from identifiers, file content from files, workspace_id from external_extract_metadata
Freshness/hash reader: SELECTs files.hash and external_extract_metadata.hash_algorithm
Long-lived poll reader: SELECTs MAX(revision) from canonical_revisions and the delta from revision_file_changes
Cheap status reader: COUNT and DISTINCT file_path from symbols
Miller's OWN in-memory BM25 inverted index — proves Miller builds search itself, does not read julie FTS

Test fixture transcribing julie's schema.rs DDL verbatim (schema 28); authoritative column shapes for files, symbols, identifiers, relationships, type_arguments, literals, symbol_annotations, schema_version, external_extract_metadata, canonical_revisions, revision_file_changes
Miller-OWNED workspaces table (~/.miller/workspaces.db) — NOT a julie table; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workspaces
Miller-OWNED tool_telemetry table — NOT a julie table; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tool_telemetry

contract_points: JulieSchemaGate.Verify(connection) is the single compatibility gate, run on an open Mode=ReadOnly connection BEFORE any bulk read. It REQUIRES three tables to exist and gates three values: (1) schema_version table — COALESCE(MAX(version),0) must equal 28; (2) external_extract_metadata table — key 'extract_contract_version' must parse to 3, key 'hash_algorithm' must equal 'blake3'. Missing table or missing key throws IncompatibleExtractException. (JulieSchemaGate.cs:24-55)

REQUIRED-to-exist tables for the gate: schema_version (column: version), external_extract_metadata (columns: key, value). A missing row for hash_algorithm or extract_contract_version is treated as incompatible. (JulieSchemaGate.cs:60-110)

external_extract_metadata is a key/value table (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL). Keys Miller reads: 'extract_contract_version' (gate), 'hash_algorithm' (gate + freshness), 'workspace_id' (telemetry scoping). (JulieDbFixture.cs:817-823; JulieSchemaGate.cs:79/49; ExtractReader.cs:240; ExtractFileHashReader.cs:28)

Pinned contract constants (MillerExtractContract.cs): schema version = 28, extract_contract_version = 3, hash_algorithm = 'blake3', julie-server = v7.13.2. Bumping julie's schema/contract is a one-line change here.

files table key column is `path` (TEXT PRIMARY KEY, forward-slashed workspace-relative). Miller looks files up by path and depends on files.hash (TEXT NOT NULL, raw-byte BLAKE3) and files.content (TEXT, nullable — julie's UTF-8 snapshot). (JulieDbFixture.cs:684-697; ExtractFileHashReader.cs:17; ExtractReader.cs:249)

symbols table key column is `id` (TEXT, opaque). Miller's DocId ordering is LOCKED to ORDER BY file_path, start_line, id and the SELECT column order maps positionally to GetX ordinals — reordering julie's output or the SELECT would corrupt the projection. (SqliteSymbolReader.cs:39-61)

symbols.metadata is julie's compact serde JSON; Miller depends on two keys written by julie's test_detection.rs across all 34+ languages: is_test (bool, only present when true) and test_role (string e.g. unit/integration/e2e). A malformed/absent value degrades to (false, null) — advisory, never throws. (SqliteSymbolReader.cs:84-127)

Byte offsets (start_byte, end_byte, body_start_byte, body_end_byte) are absolute UTF-8 byte indices; lines (start_line, end_line, body_*_line) are 1-based. Miller slices files.content on UTF-8 bytes per this contract. (ExtractReader.cs:15-16, 255-267)

identifiers.target_symbol_id is unused by design (always NULL at extract); Miller resolves references/edges by NAME, accepting homonym over-approximation. Edge building unions relationships (by-id, precise) with identifiers (name-resolved, dense). (SymbolDetail.cs:18-21; SymbolGraphReader.cs:9-29)

revision_file_changes.change_kind is CHECK-constrained to {added, modified, deleted}; Miller throws InvalidOperationException on any other value (treats it as schema drift). (FreshnessReader.cs:118-126; JulieDbFixture.cs:848)

Freshness cursor contract: MAX(revision) FROM canonical_revisions WHERE workspace_id=? returns 0 for no-revision; the no-lingering-transaction discipline (auto-commit per query, no open txn) lets a single long-lived read connection observe julie-server's WAL commits without reopening. (FreshnessReader.cs:61-81, 26-39)

Search is NOT delegated to julie — Miller owns tokenization, postings, and BM25 ranking in MillerSearchIndex (K1=1.2, B=0.75, exact-name boost 1.5) built from the symbols projection. Miller does not depend on any julie FTS5/MATCH/porter artifact. (MillerSearchIndex.cs:6-19, 51)

DbSet<T> bridge anchor: Miller treats symbols rows with kind='property' and signature LIKE '%DbSet<%' as EF entity↔table breadcrumbs (property name = table, generic arg = entity). Depends on julie populating symbols.signature for properties. (SqliteBridgeReader.cs:163-194)

WAL sidecar trap: Miller opens Mode=ReadOnly (NOT immutable=1) via SqliteReadOnlyAccess.Open and probes the DB directory for writability up front — a non-writable directory is surfaced as InvalidOperationException, not a mid-stream SQLITE_READONLY. Miller does not write to julie's DB. (SqliteSymbolReader.cs:10-16, 33-34)

Tables Miller CREATEs and owns (NOT julie's extract, excluded from this dependency surface): `workspaces` in ~/.miller/workspaces.db (registry) and `tool_telemetry` in the telemetry DB. (WorkspaceRegistry.cs:9; TelemetryLedger.cs:19)
risks: Positional SELECT-to-ordinal coupling: SqliteSymbolReader and the bridge/graph readers map columns by GetInt32/GetString ordinal, not by name. If julie ever changes column ORDER (not just adds columns) in symbols/identifiers/literals/type_arguments/symbol_annotations/relationships, Miller silently mis-reads values with no gate to catch it — the gate only checks schema/contract version numbers, not column layout.

The DDL column shapes used here come from the test fixture JulieDbFixture.cs ('transcribed verbatim from julie src/database/schema.rs', schema 28 / v7.13.1-7.13.2). The live julie DB was NOT inspected in this session (the julie-extractors repo's schema lives elsewhere and this task is Miller-only). If the fixture has drifted from the real binary, the column inventory could be slightly off — but every column Miller actually SELECTs is verified against the reader source, which is authoritative for the dependency.

symbols.metadata is_test/test_role parsing is keyed on julie's exact JSON key spelling and the convention that is_test is only emitted when true. If julie changes to emitting is_test:false explicitly or renames test_role, Miller's cheap ordinal pre-filter still works but a renamed key would silently make all symbols non-tests (advisory, no error).

Fixture comment at SqliteBridgeReader/JulieDbFixture references 'v7.13.1' in places while MillerExtractContract pins v7.13.2 — version strings in comments are slightly inconsistent, though the gate constant (7.13.2 / schema 28 / contract 3) is the single binding value.
open_questions: Does the real pinned julie-server v7.13.2 DB column order for symbols/identifiers exactly match JulieDbFixture.cs? Confirming would require dumping `.schema` against a live `extract scan` output (the julie-extractors repo, off-limits this session) — Miller has no name-based column gate, so order matters.

Is identifiers.target_symbol_id ever populated by a julie analyze pass that Miller could consume to drop the homonym over-approximation? Code comments say it is NULL at extract 'until julie's analyze pass resolves' it, implying a future julie capability Miller does not yet read.

map.area: Miller PACKAGING / binary acquisition for julie-server
map.summary: Miller does not parse source; it delegates extraction to a pinned julie-server binary obtained out-of-band by scripts/restore-julie-server.sh (Unix) and .ps1 (Windows). Both scripts read scripts/julie-pins.json for the version (7.13.2), per-platform asset name + committed sha256, and a URL template pointing at GitHub release assets of anortham/julie. They detect the host triple, download the .tar.gz/.zip from github.com/anortham/julie/releases/download/v7.13.2/, verify sha256 (julie publishes no checksum assets, so pins are download-verified-and-committed), extract ONLY julie-server from a flat multi-binary archive, set exec/clear quarantine, and delete the archive. A --from-source / MILLER_JULIE_SOURCE path builds from a local Julie cargo checkout instead. At build time Miller.Server.csproj copies repo-root .tools/julie-server next to the output binary; at runtime WorkspaceContext.ToolsRoot = AppContext.BaseDirectory/.tools and JulieExtractRunner.Locate resolves julie-server[.exe] there then on PATH. The only --version assertion is inside the restore scripts (during install); the running .NET code never invokes --version and instead gates on the DB schema (28) / extract_contract_version (3) / hash_algorithm (blake3), not the binary's version string.

contract_points: Pin source of truth is scripts/julie-pins.json with keys: version (string), urlTemplate (with {VER} and {asset} placeholders), assets.<triple>.name, assets.<triple>.sha256. Bumping the binary = edit this JSON + MillerExtractContract constants.
Release URL pattern: https://github.com/anortham/julie/releases/download/v<version>/<asset> against the anortham/julie repo.

Asset naming convention: julie-v<version>-<rust-triple>.tar.gz for darwin/linux, julie-v<version>-<rust-triple>.zip for windows. Supported triples: aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc only.
Archive is a FLAT multi-binary bundle containing julie-server (+ julie-adapter + julie-daemon at top level); the consumer must extract by exact member name 'julie-server' / 'julie-server.exe'.
No upstream checksum asset exists; sha256 is hand-committed in pins and verified by the restore scripts (mismatch deletes file + exits non-zero).
Runtime binary location: AppContext.BaseDirectory/.tools/julie-server (non-Windows) or julie-server.exe (Windows). Build-time Content copy places it there from repo-root ../../.tools/julie-server.
Resolution order at runtime: ToolsRoot/.tools first, then PATH (FindOnPath); absence throws FileNotFoundException referencing scripts/restore-julie-server.sh|.ps1 and v7.13.2.

from-source override: pass --from-source (sh) / -FromSource (ps1) or set MILLER_JULIE_SOURCE=/path/to/julie checkout; requires Cargo.toml + cargo; runs `cargo build --manifest-path <root>/Cargo.toml --bin julie-server --release` and copies target/release/julie-server[.exe].

Runtime version compatibility is gated on the EXTRACT DB/REPORT (schema_version=28, extract_contract_version=3, hash_algorithm=blake3 in MillerExtractContract), NOT on the binary's --version string. The --version assertion exists ONLY in the restore scripts at install time.

The build's Content copy is conditioned on Exists(...) so a no-restore machine still builds; runtime then fails loudly. After copy, EnsureJulieServerExecutable target re-applies chmod +x on non-Windows because MSBuild Copy drops the exec bit.
Exec bit + macOS quarantine handling: sh restore does chmod +x and xattr -d com.apple.quarantine; the csproj re-chmods the output copy. Process.Start would EACCES without these.
risks: The four committed sha256 pins are trust anchors with no upstream checksum cross-reference; if a pin is wrong or the release asset is re-uploaded, every download fails (or, if a pin were maliciously edited, integrity is only as good as the commit). No signature verification, only sha256.

Restore scripts assert the binary --version, but the live .NET runtime does NOT — a binary whose --version drifts from 7.13.2 but still writes schema 28 / contract 3 / blake3 would be accepted at runtime. Conversely a correct-version binary producing a drifted DB is caught. The binary-vs-DB version coupling is implicit, not enforced in-process.
linux-arm64 and windows-arm64 have no prebuilt asset; those hosts MUST use --from-source (needs a full Julie cargo checkout + Rust toolchain), which is a heavier prerequisite than a download.

The Windows .ps1 uses Expand-Archive + recursive Get-ChildItem -Filter 'julie-server.exe' (first match), assuming the .zip layout; the .sh assumes a flat tar member named exactly 'julie-server'. If upstream changes archive layout (e.g. nested dir), the .sh `tar ... julie-server` extraction breaks while the .ps1 recursive search would still find it — divergent fragility between the two scripts.

The ~77MB binary is copied per build (PreserveNewest mitigates recopy when unchanged), and is gitignored, so a fresh clone with no restore builds but is non-functional until restore runs — easy to miss in CI lanes that only run the fast suite.
open_questions: Whether anortham/julie actually publishes v7.13.2 release assets yet — the script comments and CLAUDE.md repeatedly reference a window 'before GitHub release assets publish' where --from-source is required; I did not (and per rules cannot) hit the network to confirm the assets exist live.

Whether julie's release archive truly contains julie-server/julie-adapter/julie-daemon at the FLAT top level for all 4 triples — this is asserted in the script comments and relied on by `tar ... julie-server`, but I verified it only from Miller-side comments, not by inspecting an actual upstream archive.

Exact julie-server --version output format — the scripts match a substring ' <version>' (sh grep -F " ${VERSION}") / '* <version>*' (ps1 -like); the precise banner string lives in the julie-extractors repo, which the Miller index does not cover and was out of scope to read.

Symbol read SELECT (deterministic DocId ordering): SELECT id, name, signature, kind, language, file_path, start_line, parent_id FROM symbols WHERE name IS NOT NULL ORDER BY file_path, start_line, id;

symbols.id and identifiers.id are opaque lowercase 32-char MD5 hex over an 8-field span ({file_path}:{name}:{start_line}:{start_col}:{end_line}:{end_col}:{start_byte}:{end_byte}); IDs churn on any byte-offset-shifting edit; treat as opaque, never cache resolved links across file updates.
identifiers.target_symbol_id is ALWAYS NULL from extract (consumer resolves); identifiers.containing_symbol_id IS populated.

symbols.file_hash always NULL; symbols.semantic_group never populated; symbols.reference_score 0.0 unless --analyze ran and external_extract_metadata.analysis_state=='current'. Freshness uses files.hash (BLAKE3 hex) + files.last_modified.
No FTS5 / no *_fts tables exist (dropped in migration 007). Miller builds its own in-memory BM25 index; do not query any *_fts table.
relationships is sparse and within-language only; not usable for cross-language links. Cross-language must be derived from identifiers + signatures.
File paths in the DB are relative unix-style to external_extract_metadata.root_path; must be joined to root_path for absolute and normalized to forward slashes.

CLI: julie-server extract --db <ABS_DB> --root <ABS_ROOT> --json <scan|update|delete|analyze|info>. --db required for all; --root required for scan/update/delete. --json is mandatory (default output is unparseable TEXT, still exit 0). Use ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList, absolute paths, no shell.

Exit-code mapping: 0 → stdout JSON ExtractReport (status scanned/rebuilt/changed/unchanged/ignored/deleted/not_found/analyzed); 1 → stdout JSON ExtractReport with status='failed' + errors[]; 2 → no stdout, clap usage text on stderr (NOT JSON). Capture stdout and stderr separately; parse only stdout as JSON.

First call on a fresh DB MUST be scan (binds workspace_id + root, writes metadata); update/delete/analyze/info on a metadata-less DB → exit 1. Miller must Directory.CreateDirectory the --db parent (julie does not mkdir).

Single-writer constraint: each extract op takes a 30s exclusive flock on <db>.julie-extract.lock; Miller must serialize writers. info opens read-only and takes NO flock (safe under a concurrent writer).

ExtractReport JSON field names use serde snake_case with db→db_path rename; info counts arrive flat as files_total/symbols_total/relationships_total/identifiers_total/types_total (ulong), not nested. schema_state ∈ missing|older|current|newer.
delete of an absent file is tolerant: status='not_found', exit 0 — NOT a failure. update on a now-ignored file silently becomes a delete: status='ignored'.

map.area: What Miller's MCP tools read from the index to serve users (DB-table/column backing of search/inspect/trace/impact/context/edit/workspace)
map.summary: Miller is a read-only consumer of a pinned julie-server SQLite extract (julie-server v7.13.2, schema 28, extract_contract_version 3, hash_algorithm=blake3). At startup/rebuild, RepositoryIndexLoader.Load reads three table-groups once and builds ONE immutable in-memory unit: (a) a BM25 inverted index over symbols.name + symbols.signature (Miller builds this itself in MillerSearchIndex — there is NO SQLite FTS5/MATCH table anywhere; grep for fts/MATCH/virtual table found zero query usage); (b) a directed dependency SymbolGraph from relationships (by-id) UNION identifiers (name-resolved, homonym over-approximation because identifiers.target_symbol_id is always NULL at extract); (c) a cross-language BridgeGraph from type_arguments, literals, symbol_annotations, and symbols rows with kind='property' + signature LIKE '%DbSet<%'. search/context/trace/impact run entirely against these in-memory structures (no per-call DB). inspect (depth=full) and edit are the only tools that hit the DB per-call via ExtractReader, reading symbols (doc/visibility/body byte+line spans, edit spans) and identifiers (references, callees where kind='call', rename byte sites) plus files.content for body/edit text. Freshness uses canonical_revisions, revision_file_changes, files.hash, and external_extract_metadata. Several julie-specific columns/computed fields are load-bearing: symbols.metadata JSON (is_test, test_role), files.hash + hash_algorithm=blake3, the revision tables, and the symbol-id join key — a v1 schema rename/drop of any of these breaks specific tools.

Indexing carrier: SymbolId (julie opaque MD5-hex join key), ParentId, IsTest, TestRole from symbols.metadata

contract_points: search ranking input = symbols.name concatenated with symbols.signature; a v1 schema must keep both columns populated or BM25 quality silently degrades (signature is optional but contributes terms).

search/inspect/impact/context test-aware behavior depends on symbols.metadata being JSON containing keys 'is_test' (bool, only emitted when true) and 'test_role' (string). Miller substring-probes the raw metadata text before parsing (SqliteSymbolReader.cs:96-99) — renaming these keys or moving them to a typed column breaks test hiding (search), the impact 'likely tests' partition, and trace seeds.

Dependency graph (trace auto/path, impact, context expansion) requires `relationships`(from_symbol_id, to_symbol_id, kind) and `identifiers`(name, kind, containing_symbol_id). identifiers.target_symbol_id is read by NO query — Miller assumes it is always NULL and resolves edges by name. If v1 starts populating target_symbol_id, Miller would NOT use it without code changes (it still name-resolves), keeping homonym over-approximation.

inspect depth=full and the whole edit pipeline depend on per-symbol byte+line spans on the `symbols` table: doc_comment, visibility, code_context, start_byte, end_byte, body_start_byte, body_end_byte, body_start_line, body_end_line, start_line. Body/edit slicing assumes byte offsets are absolute UTF-8 byte indices and lines are 1-based.

inspect references/callees and edit rename read `identifiers`(name, kind, file_path, start_line, start_byte, end_byte, containing_symbol_id). callees specifically filter kind='call' (string literal). Rename byte sites require non-NULL start_byte/end_byte.

trace mode=bridge requires four sources with these exact column shapes: type_arguments(identifier_id, ordinal, parent_arg_id, type_name, file_path); literals(literal_text, kind, carrier, arg_position, language, containing_symbol_id, start_byte, end_byte, file_path, start_line); symbol_annotations(symbol_id, ordinal, annotation, annotation_key, raw_text, carrier); and the EF convention symbols rows kind='property' with signature LIKE '%DbSet<%' (property name = table, generic arg = entity). No dedicated bridge/edge-confidence columns are read — bridge scores/bands are computed in Miller.Core, not stored by julie.

Body/edit text source is `files`(path, content) and edit freshness is `files`(path, hash) gated by external_extract_metadata.hash_algorithm='blake3' (raw-byte BLAKE3). content is read verbatim as TEXT.

Freshness/refresh require `canonical_revisions`(revision, workspace_id) and `revision_file_changes`(revision, file_path, change_kind, workspace_id) with change_kind CHECK-constrained to exactly {added,modified,deleted} — an unknown value throws (FreshnessReader.cs:118-126).

Schema gate requires `schema_version`(version) and `external_extract_metadata`(key,value) with keys extract_contract_version and hash_algorithm and value 'workspace_id'. Pinned to schema 28 / contract 3 / blake3 / julie-server 7.13.2 in MillerExtractContract.cs (one-line bump point).

The opaque symbol id (julie MD5-hex) is the universal join key across symbols.id, symbols.parent_id, identifiers.containing_symbol_id, relationships.from/to_symbol_id, type_arguments.identifier_id, symbol_annotations.symbol_id. A v1 that changes id encoding/stability must keep it consistent across ALL these tables or every graph/detail join breaks.

Reader contract: SqliteSymbolReader SELECT order is (file_path, start_line, id) and the 0-based row ordinal becomes DocId; MillerRepositoryIndex validates DocId==ordinal and throws on drift (MillerRepositoryIndex.cs:168-171).
risks: Negative-claim caveat (verified): I grepped src/**/*.cs for fts|MATCH|virtual table|fts5|bm25 and found NO SQL FTS usage — search is purely Miller's in-memory BM25. This is positively confirmed by MillerSearchIndex.cs, not just absence.

A v1 schema that renames symbols.metadata keys (is_test/test_role) or types them as columns would SILENTLY degrade rather than error: ParseTestSignals returns (false,null) on any miss (SqliteSymbolReader.cs:96-99,122-126), so tests would stop being hidden/partitioned with no failure signal.

identifiers.target_symbol_id being NULL is a structural assumption baked into edges, references, callees, and rename. If v1 names cross-references differently (e.g. a resolved reference table), Miller's name-based resolution would either miss precise edges or keep over-approximating; trace/impact precision is capped by this.

Bridge detection leans on string conventions not stored signals: symbol_annotations.annotation values for HTTP verbs/[Route], and signature LIKE '%DbSet<%'. A v1 that normalizes annotations into typed columns or changes signature formatting would break trace mode=bridge without a schema-version bump catching it (the gate only checks schema/contract/hash, not these column semantics).

Freshness depends on workspace_id partitioning in canonical_revisions/revision_file_changes AND on files.hash being raw-byte BLAKE3. A v1 that changes the hash algorithm value (not 'blake3') hard-fails the schema gate (good), but a v1 that changes hashing semantics while keeping the label would cause false stale/fresh verdicts on edit.

No reference/relevance score column is read from the DB at all — search score (BM25) and bridge confidence/band are computed in Miller.Core. A v1 that ships precomputed scores would be ignored unless wired in; conversely Miller does not depend on any stored score, so dropping such columns is safe.
open_questions: Does the new product's schema-v1 keep symbols.metadata as a JSON blob, or promote is_test/test_role to typed columns? Miller's substring-probe + JSON parse (SqliteSymbolReader.ParseTestSignals) would need rework either way; verify against the v1 symbols DDL.

Will v1 populate identifiers.target_symbol_id (resolved cross-references)? If so, Miller could replace name-based edge/rename resolution with precise id joins — but currently it ignores the column entirely.

Does v1 retain the EF DbSet<T> + symbol_annotations conventions the bridge depends on, or move route/verb/entity-table linkage into dedicated relationship rows? The bridge reader (SqliteBridgeReader) is the most convention-fragile consumer.

Are the byte-span columns (start_byte/end_byte/body_start_byte/body_end_byte) and files.content guaranteed in v1 with the same absolute-UTF-8-byte / 1-based-line semantics? inspect(full) body and ALL edit ops splice on these.

Does v1 keep the canonical_revisions / revision_file_changes freshness tables and the workspace_id keying, or replace the freshness model? FreshnessReader and the edit freshness gate are tightly coupled to these.

I did not open Miller.Core/Graph/BridgeGraph.cs, BridgeGraphBuilder.cs, or the Core resolver/scorer files in full — they are pure (no DB), so they read NO tables, but if the synthesis needs the exact bridge scoring inputs those files hold the computation (confirmed DB-free by RepositoryIndexLoader passing already-read rows in).

map.summary: The implemented CLI matches the contract doc closely. The binary is named `julie-extract`, defined as a `[[bin]]` in crates/julie-extract-cli/Cargo.toml (package name `julie-extract-cli`, version 0.1.0), built with `cargo build -p julie-extract-cli --bin julie-extract`. All six documented subcommands (scan, update, delete, info, export, languages) exist in code (args.rs `Command` enum + dispatch in commands.rs `run`). Flags match the contract exactly, including the repeatable `--ignore-file` (clap field `ignore_files`) and `--strict-schema`/`--json`/`--force`. One real divergence from the contract narrative: path-policy "typed errors" like FileOutsideRoot return exit code 1, not 3, even though the doc lists "file outside root" and "root mismatch" together as typed errors (root mismatch IS exit 3; file-outside-root is exit 1).

Without --json: stdout/stderr carry only a bare status word (ok/no_change/unsupported/not_found/partial/failed) and human text is explicitly NOT a stable contract.

Exit codes: 0 = ok including no_change/unsupported/not_found; 1 = runtime op failure (extract/export/artifact) AND path-policy errors (invalid path, file-outside-root, file-not-found); 2 = clap usage error; 3 = incompatible schema/root/contract or --strict-schema migration-required.

Report JSON top-level shape includes report_schema_version (=1), status, operation, mode, tool.binary_name (="julie-extract"), artifact, revision, counts, errors[], languages (for `languages`). errors[].code is the stable machine code (e.g. unsupported_format, schema_incompatible, root_mismatch, file_outside_root, file_not_found).

In code, RootMismatch is exit 3 (matches) but FileOutsideRoot / InvalidPath / FileNotFound (FileNotFound also documented as `failed` with file_not_found) all return exit 1, not 3. A consumer keying off exit code alone cannot distinguish a path error (1) from an extraction failure (1); it must read errors[].code. This is consistent with the contract's stated principle that exit codes are coarse and the JSON code is the precise contract, but the prose 'typed error' wording could mislead.
`--out` is typed `PathBuf` and the stdout sentinel is the literal `-` compared via `Path::new("-")`. A consumer must pass exactly `-` (not an empty string) to trigger stdout streaming.
Human (non-JSON) output is explicitly unstable; any Miller code that ever parses non-JSON stdout would be relying on non-contract behavior.
open_questions: The contract's 'Open decision' about a caller-supplied artifact_id flag remains unimplemented: no `--artifact-id` (or similar) flag exists in args.rs; artifact_id is generated internally (new_artifact_metadata -> generated_artifact_id). Confirmed by absence in the arg structs.

`update` on a missing file is documented to return `failed` with `file_not_found`; in code canonicalize_update_file yields PathPolicyError::FileNotFound -> path_error_diagnostic maps to ReportCode::FileNotFound with exit 1 and status Failed. Whether downstream treats this as a hard failure vs a signal-to-delete is a consumer policy not enforced by the CLI.

map.summary: The implemented schema in crates/julie-extract-artifact/src/schema.rs (const SCHEMA_SQL, executed by create_schema) is a byte-for-byte match to docs/contracts/sqlite-schema-v1.md: 18 public tables and 17 required indexes, identical column lists, ordering, types, nullability, PKs and FKs. The only deltas vs the doc are cosmetic and intentional: code uses CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS (doc omits IF NOT EXISTS) and adds a leading PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON. No table or column exists in code that is absent from the doc, and none in the doc is missing from code. The metadata table is artifact_metadata(key,value) with 11 required keys enforced via REQUIRED_METADATA_KEYS; file hash column is files.content_hash storing a blake3:<hex> string with artifact_metadata.hash_algorithm = "blake3"; the symbols JSON-blob column is metadata_json (every table uses metadata_json, never a bare "metadata"). IDs are opaque text: symbol_id is a bare 32-char MD5 hex (NO prefix), while file_id and several artifact-generated IDs use a "{prefix}-{first32hex-of-blake3}" form (e.g. file-, type_fact-) and artifact_id is "artifact-{nanos}" — there is NO sym_/file_ underscore-prefix scheme. There is definitively NO FTS/search table, NO embeddings table, and NO test-quality/reference-score table anywhere in the crate; a contract test actively asserts those forbidden tables are absent.

map.summary: julie-extractors ships a binary named `julie-extract` (NOT `julie-server`) at version 0.1.0 from a separate repo (`github.com/murphy/julie-extractors`, per workspace Cargo.toml). Its release path is intentionally NOT a publishable distribution yet: the `Release Binaries` GitHub Actions workflow stages a per-target package DIRECTORY (binary + SHA-256 sidecar + contract/release docs) and uploads it ONLY as a GitHub Actions artifact — no GitHub Release, no attached release assets, no tarball/zip, and no checksum-of-archive. The package is produced by `cargo xtask release package`. The binary is fully self-contained (statically links tree-sitter grammars as compiled C, bundles SQLite via rusqlite `bundled`; macOS binary links only libSystem), so no grammars or shared libs ship alongside it. CRITICAL MISMATCH for Miller: Miller's restore pipeline (`scripts/restore-julie-server.sh` + `julie-pins.json`) pins `julie-server v7.13.2` from `anortham/julie` as flat multi-binary `.tar.gz`/`.zip` release-download assets — a completely different product, repo, version scheme, binary name, and asset layout than what julie-extractors produces. There is currently no mechanism for Miller to obtain `julie-extract` from julie-extractors at all (no published assets, and the names/repos don't line up).

Version detection options for a consumer: (a) `julie-extract --version` -> `julie-extract 0.1.0` (clap name+version); (b) any `--json` report's `tool.binary_version` -> bare `0.1.0`; (c) SQLite `artifact_metadata.binary_version` -> bare `0.1.0`. Contract versions a consumer pins against: extract_contract_version=1, sqlite_schema_version=1 (== schema_version), jsonl_schema_version=1, report_schema_version=1, hash_algorithm=`blake3`. All present in artifact_metadata and in JSON reports.

Package layout (per target): `dist/{target}/julie-extract{exe_suffix}` + `dist/{target}/julie-extract{exe_suffix}.sha256` + contract/arch/testing/release docs + `docs/release-notes/v{version}.md`. Checksum sidecar line format: `{sha256hex}  dist/{target}/julie-extract{exe_suffix}` (two-space separator, posix path).

Distribution is currently a GitHub Actions ARTIFACT directory named `julie-extract-v{version}-{target}`, NOT a release asset and NOT an archive. There is no URL a script can download from without going through the Actions API and manual promotion.

Supported target triples: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. Note Miller's restore expects FOUR triples including x86_64-apple-darwin and a linux x86_64 — julie-extractors does NOT build x86_64-apple-darwin (only aarch64).
Binary is statically self-contained (tree-sitter grammars compiled in, SQLite bundled). A consumer needs only the single binary file; no grammar files, no shared libs, no extra runtime to ship.
`cargo xtask release package-list` emits a tab-separated `kind\tpath_template` manifest a consumer/CI can read to know exactly what a package contains.

To pin a version today, a consumer can only: build from source at a tagged commit (`cargo build --release -p julie-extract-cli --bin julie-extract`) or run the staging command for a given `--version`/`--target`. There is no published, checksummed, downloadable asset to pin by URL+sha256 the way Miller pins julie-server.
risks: PRODUCT/NAMING MISMATCH: Miller pins `julie-server` 7.13.2 from anortham/julie; julie-extractors produces `julie-extract` 0.1.0 from murphy/julie-extractors. These are different binaries, repos, and version schemes. If the intent is for Miller to consume julie-extractors, the entire restore pipeline (pins file, asset names, urlTemplate, binary name, extraction logic) must change. As-is, Miller cannot obtain julie-extract.

NO PUBLISHED ASSETS: julie-extractors deliberately does not publish GitHub Releases or attach assets (release.md:94, v0.1.0.md status). Miller's restore model (download by URL, verify sha256) has nothing to point at. Blocking for any download-based pin until julie-extractors starts publishing release assets.

NO ARCHIVE: julie-extractors stages a directory, not a tarball/zip. Miller's restore expects `tar -xzf`/`Expand-Archive` of an archive containing the binary. A directory artifact is not consumable by that code path.

TARGET TRIPLE GAP: Miller supports/expects x86_64-apple-darwin and a linux x86_64 archive; julie-extractors macOS build is aarch64-apple-darwin only and uses x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu — partial overlap, plus no x86_64-apple-darwin (Intel Mac) coverage from julie-extractors.

VERSION-STRING INCONSISTENCY (verified bug): test fixtures assert `binary_version == "julie-extract 0.1.0"` (schema_contract.rs:122, cli_contract.rs:253) but the live JSON `tool.binary_version` and persisted artifact_metadata.binary_version are bare `0.1.0`. A consumer parsing `tool.binary_version` expecting the `julie-extract ` prefix (as the fixtures suggest) will mismatch. The fixtures encode the clap `--version` string, not the structured field.

NO CHECKSUM-OF-ARCHIVE / NO SIGNATURE: only a per-binary .sha256 sidecar is produced. There is no signed release, no archive digest. A download-and-verify pin would have to checksum the raw binary, not an archive.

REPOSITORY URL LOOKS LIKE A PLACEHOLDER: Cargo.toml repository is github.com/murphy/julie-extractors while the real Julie org is anortham. If this repo is meant to publish assets, the repo slug for any urlTemplate is currently undefined/likely wrong.
open_questions: Is julie-extractors actually intended to replace julie-server as Miller's extraction backend, or is it a parallel product? Miller's M1 design and pins reference julie-server 7.13.2 / schema 26, while julie-extractors is julie-extract 0.1.0 / sqlite_schema_version 1 — the schema version numbers also differ, suggesting Miller is NOT yet wired to julie-extractors at all.
When (if ever) will julie-extractors publish downloadable, checksummed release assets, and under what repo slug + asset naming? Without that, Miller cannot adopt a download-based pin.
Will julie-extractors ship archives (tar.gz/zip) or stay directory-only? Miller's restore code assumes archives.
Will julie-extractors add an x86_64-apple-darwin target (Intel Mac) and a windows/linux-arm story, to match Miller's expected triple set?

Should the binary_version structured field be made to match the documented `julie-extract <ver>` fixture convention, or should the fixtures be corrected to bare `0.1.0`? (This is a real divergence between tests and runtime that a consumer must be told which to trust — runtime emits bare `0.1.0`.)

Does Miller's SQLite reader expect `julie-server` schema 26 columns or julie-extract sqlite_schema_version 1 columns? The schema contracts appear to be different generations; consuming julie-extract artifacts may require Miller schema changes beyond just the restore pipeline.

map.area: julie-extractors INTENDED migration story + non-goals + decisions
map.summary: julie-extractors is a deliberate standalone split of Julie's tree-sitter extraction work into a new canonical product. The intended consumption model for Miller is CLI-first (`julie-extract` binary) producing a versioned SQLite artifact (primary) plus an optional JSONL export (secondary); the contract explicitly forbids the CLI from starting a daemon, registering a workspace, building a search index, computing embeddings, running MCP tools, or watching the filesystem. The docs name Miller directly as a target consumer, generalize the CLI from "patterns Miller has proven matter," and state that everything search/ranking/embeddings/watcher/workspace-registry/analysis-test-quality is a DOWNSTREAM concern that julie-extractors will NOT own — so Miller must own anything it currently gets from the old julie-server beyond raw extraction. There is no old-julie-server schema compatibility guarantee: v1 is a clean extractor-native schema, "do not maintain old Julie compatibility mode," and Julie/Miller/Eros keep their existing paths until they migrate intentionally to the stable contract. Three open decisions are explicitly flagged in the contract docs: caller-supplied artifact id flag, direct JSONL streaming during scan (no SQLite), and exact parser version fields. The 12-task migration plan is marked complete (all checkboxes + verification ledger), and a v0.1.0 release/dogfood/perf-baseline track exists.

contract_points: CLI binary name is `julie-extract` (Task 9 acceptance, cli.md:32-39). Miller invokes it as a subprocess; this replaces `julie-server extract`.

Six v1 commands only: `scan --root <dir> --db <path> [--force] [--ignore-file <path>...] [--strict-schema] [--json]`, `update ... --file <path>`, `delete ... --file <path>`, `info --db <path>`, `export --db <path> --format jsonl --out <path|->`, `languages`. No `analyze` (cli.md:32-39; migration plan line 344).
SQLite is the primary durable artifact bound to ONE canonical root; a root mismatch is a typed error (exit code 3) unless `scan --force` rebuilds (cli.md:62-63, 144).

Stable JSON report contract gated behind `--json`: report_schema_version=1, status in {ok,no_change,unsupported,not_found,partial,failed}, plus operation/mode/input/artifact/tool/revision/counts/errors/warnings. Human (non-json) output is NOT a stable contract (cli.md:24; reports.md:14-124).
counts.rows_written and counts.totals are EXHAUSTIVE over the 18 SQLite v1 row domains; every key must be emitted with 0 when absent (reports.md:120-123).

Stable v1 error codes (reports.md:164-183): usage_error, invalid_path, file_outside_root, file_not_found, root_mismatch, schema_migration_required, schema_incompatible, contract_incompatible, db_open_failed, db_write_failed, lock_timeout, unsupported_format, unsupported_file, read_failed, parse_failed, data_loss_guard, export_failed, internal_error. These are stable API spellings.
Exit codes: 0 = completed incl. no_change/unsupported/not_found; 1 = ran but op failed; 2 = CLI usage error; 3 = incompatible artifact/schema/root/contract (cli.md:139-144).
Contract version pins all = 1: CLI contract 1, extraction contract 1, SQLite schema 1, JSONL schema 1 (cli.md:13-18). Miller should version-gate via `info` before opening.
Stored file paths are root-relative Unix-style strings; lines 1-based, columns 0-based, byte offsets 0-based UTF-8 (cli.md:59; sqlite-schema-v1.md:14-18).

artifact_metadata required keys consumers may read: artifact_id, root_path, schema_version, extract_contract_version, sqlite_schema_version, binary_version, hash_algorithm, parser_inventory_fingerprint, capability_snapshot_fingerprint, created_at, updated_at (sqlite-schema-v1.md:33-44).

18 public SQLite tables downstream readers may rely on: artifact_metadata, parser_inventory, extraction_revisions, revision_file_changes, files, symbols, symbol_annotations, identifiers, relationships, pending_relationships, type_facts, type_argument_usages, type_arguments, literals, parse_diagnostics, language_capabilities, language_capability_fixtures, language_capability_gaps (sqlite-schema-v1.md). Required indexes are contracted, not advisory (sqlite-schema-v1.md:502-525).

files.content_hash + hash_algorithm metadata (example: blake3) is the freshness signal; Miller's incremental update/delete pattern relies on hash-skip semantics (sqlite-schema-v1.md:130; performance contract line 482; reports.md:36).

JSONL export is snapshot-only in v1 with a fixed envelope {jsonl_schema_version, extract_contract_version, kind, op, artifact_id, record_id, record} and a deterministic 18-kind record order (jsonl-v1.md:12-62). `export --out - --json` puts JSONL on stdout and the report on stderr (cli.md:115-117; reports.md:241).

update semantics Miller must honor: changed->replaces rows; unchanged->no_change; unsupported/ignored->deletes stale rows + returns unsupported; missing file->failed/file_not_found (use delete instead) (cli.md:80-91).
Data-loss guard: a parser/read/extractor failure must NOT replace known-good rows with empty results; returns failed + data_loss_guard error, rows left intact (cli.md:154-161).
`--strict-schema` fails instead of migrating an older compatible artifact (opt-in strictness) (cli.md:47).

All are explicit non-goals/exclusions (vision.md:41-42, sqlite-schema-v1.md:537-542, reports.md:249-250). If Miller assumed any of these came from the extract artifact, that assumption breaks under the new product.

Miller's existing read paths against julie-server's DB will NOT transparently map; migration is intentional, not automatic (sqlite-schema-v1.md:542,546-549; reports.md:251-252).

Three contract-level open decisions are unresolved and could change the integration surface if a consumer (Miller) requests them: caller-supplied artifact id flag, scan->JSONL streaming without SQLite, exact parser version fields. Building Miller behavior that depends on a particular resolution is premature.

diff.dimension: CLI invocation & process layer: old `julie-server extract <op>` subprocess wrapper vs new `julie-extract <op>` binary
diff.old_behavior: Miller drives extraction through ONE subprocess wrapper, JulieExtractRunner (src/Miller.Indexing/JulieExtractRunner.cs). It resolves a binary named `julie-server` (`julie-server.exe` on Windows) under WorkspaceContext.ToolsRoot then PATH (line 61-68), and always invokes a SINGLE parent subcommand `extract` followed by one of four operation tokens. The exact argv (built via ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList, no shell): scan = `extract --db <ABS_DB> --root <ABS_ROOT> --workspace-id <SHA256_HEX> --json scan [--force]` (line 102-106); info = `extract --db <ABS_DB> --json info` (line 116); update = `extract --db <ABS_DB> --root <ABS_ROOT> --json update --file <ABS_FILE>` (line 145); delete = same with `delete` token. `--json` is always passed. stdout is parsed as a SINGLE flat JSON object into the `ExtractReport` record (ExtractReport.cs:12-34): keys status, operation, db_path (serde-renamed from `db`), root, schema_version, schema_state, extract_contract_version, analysis_state, files_scanned, symbols_extracted, files_total, symbols_total, relationships_total, identifiers_total, types_total, errors[], plus M3 freshness fields workspace_id, revision, files_updated, files_deleted, hash_algorithm. Exit-code mapping (Interpret, line 162-199): 0 -> parse report; 1 -> JulieExtractFailedException (re-parses the failed report's errors[] from stdout); 2 -> JulieExtractUsageException (stderr only, stdout NOT parsed); ANY OTHER code -> JulieExtractException treated as a crash. After exit 0, ExtractVersionMismatch.VerifyReport cross-checks report.SchemaVersion==28, ExtractContractVersion==3, HashAlgorithm=='blake3' (MillerExtractContract.cs:13-15) and throws IncompatibleExtractException on drift. The spawn is bare: UseShellExecute=false, CreateNoWindow=true, async stdout/stderr drain, then a `process.WaitForExit()` with NO timeout, NO CancellationToken, NO Kill, NO WorkingDirectory, NO env manipulation (line 274-324). IExtractOps/JulieExtractOps expose Update(path)/Delete(path)/Scan(force) and route to runner.Update/Delete/Scan with canonical (symlink-resolved) db/root/file passed verbatim.
diff.new_behavior: The new product ships a binary named `julie-extract` (crates/julie-extract-cli/Cargo.toml `[[bin]] name = "julie-extract"`; clap `#[command(name = "julie-extract")]` args.rs:7). There is NO `julie-server` binary and NO `extract` PARENT subcommand: the six operations are TOP-LEVEL clap subcommands — `scan`, `update`, `delete`, `info`, `export`, `languages` (args.rs:16-24, dispatched commands.rs:70-79). There is NO `--workspace-id` flag anywhere in any arg struct (args.rs:26-100); the artifact is bound to ONE canonical root and carries an internally-generated `artifact_id` instead. Flags per command: scan `--root --db [--force] [--ignore-file ...] [--strict-schema] [--json]`; update `--root --db --file [--ignore-file ...] [--strict-schema] [--json]`; delete `--root --db --file [--strict-schema] [--json]`; info `--db [--strict-schema] [--json]`; export `--db --format jsonl --out <path|-> [--strict-schema] [--json]`; languages `[--json]`. With `--json`, the report is written as ONE serde_json line (commands.rs:2022-2025) to stdout — EXCEPT the special case `export --out -`, where JSONL owns stdout and the JSON report is redirected to STDERR (write_outcome commands.rs:2006-2020 via ReportStream::Stderr). The report is a DIFFERENT, NESTED shape (reports.rs:28-66): top-level keys report_schema_version(=1), status, operation, mode, input{db_path,root_path,file_path,root_relative_path,format,output_path}, artifact{db_path,root_path,artifact_id,schema_version,extract_contract_version,sqlite_schema_version,jsonl_schema_version,hash_algorithm,parser_inventory_fingerprint,capability_snapshot_fingerprint} (nullable), tool{binary_name,binary_version}, revision{latest_revision_id,created_revision_id} (nullable), counts{files_scanned,files_changed,files_unchanged,files_unsupported,files_deleted,files_failed,rows_written{18 domains},totals{18 domains}}, errors[], warnings[], languages (only for `languages`). Exit codes are 0/1/2/3 (run_from_env: clap usage err -> code 2; command_error(3,...) for schema/root/contract incompatibility at commands.rs:1291-1333; path-policy errors like FileOutsideRoot return 1, root_mismatch returns 3). Versions all = 1 (SQLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION=1, EXTRACT_CONTRACT_VERSION=1, schema.rs:3-4; REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION=1). hash_algorithm is `blake3` but files.content_hash stores a PREFIXED `blake3:<hex>` string and the metadata table is `artifact_metadata` (not `external_extract_metadata`). Per-file update/delete remain (single-file ops), and `--out -` uses the literal `-` (compared via Path::new("-")) to stream JSONL to stdout.
