deltas.item: Parent `extract` subcommand removed
deltas.old: argv always starts with the token "extract" then the operation (e.g. `extract ... scan`) — JulieExtractRunner.cs:103,116,145
deltas.new: operations are top-level subcommands; argv must start with `scan`/`update`/`delete`/`info` directly (args.rs:16-24, commands.rs:70-79). Passing `extract` first yields a clap usage error (exit 2).
deltas.impact: Every BuildScanArgs/BuildInfoArgs/BuildUpdateArgs/BuildFileOpArgs must drop the leading "extract" element or all calls fail with exit 2.

deltas.item: `--workspace-id` flag removed
deltas.old: scan passes `--workspace-id <SHA256_HEX>` computed by WorkspaceId.FromCanonicalRoot (JulieExtractRunner.cs:103, WorkspaceId.cs:13)
deltas.new: no `--workspace-id` flag exists on any subcommand (args.rs ScanArgs:26-40); artifact gets an internal generated artifact_id (`artifact-<nanos>`) and is bound to one canonical root
deltas.impact: Passing `--workspace-id` produces a clap usage error (exit 2). The flag must be removed from BuildScanArgs. Miller's stable SHA-256 workspace_id is now Miller-side-only; it can no longer be pushed into julie's metadata, breaking the persisted-id cross-check / force-rebind logic in the bootstrap (DecideBootstrapScan reads external_extract_metadata.workspace_id, which no longer exists).

deltas.item: Report JSON shape (flat -> nested)
deltas.old: flat ExtractReport: status/operation/db_path/schema_version/extract_contract_version/files_total/symbols_total/.../hash_algorithm/errors[] (ExtractReport.cs:12-34)
deltas.new: nested Report: report_schema_version/status/operation/mode/input{}/artifact{schema_version,extract_contract_version,sqlite_schema_version,hash_algorithm,artifact_id,...}/tool{binary_name,binary_version}/revision{latest_revision_id,created_revision_id}/counts{...,rows_written{18},totals{18}}/errors[]/warnings[]/languages (reports.rs:28-66,112-180)
deltas.impact: Deserializing the new report into Miller's ExtractReport leaves nearly every field null/0: schema_version/extract_contract_version/hash_algorithm now live under `artifact`, not at top level — so ExtractVersionMismatch.VerifyReport reads nulls and (per its skip-null policy) silently passes, defeating the version gate. Counts (files_scanned etc.) move under `counts`. The whole ExtractReport record and ParseReport must be rewritten to the nested shape.

deltas.item: Error record shape
deltas.old: ExtractError{code,message,path} (ExtractReport.cs:37-40); errors[] re-parsed from stdout on exit 1 (JulieExtractRunner.cs:178)
deltas.new: ReportDiagnostic{code,message,path,root_relative_path,recoverable,details} (reports.rs:299-307); also a separate warnings[] array. code is a snake_case enum with a different/expanded set (reports.rs:250-274): adds data_loss_guard, lock_timeout(was flock_timeout), file_outside_root, root_mismatch, schema_incompatible, contract_incompatible, db_open_failed, db_write_failed, unsupported_format, etc.
deltas.impact: ExtractError gains optional fields (recoverable is a first-class signal Miller currently lacks). IndexerCore's TransientErrorCodes set {data_loss_guard, flock_timeout} is partly stale: the new code is `lock_timeout` not `flock_timeout`, so transient lock contention would misroute to ERROR. Should switch to the `recoverable` flag and/or the new code spellings.

deltas.item: Exit-code contract gains code 3
deltas.old: Interpret maps 0/1/2 explicitly; ANY other code (incl. 3) -> JulieExtractException 'unexpected code' = treated as a crash (JulieExtractRunner.cs:195-197)
deltas.new: exit 3 is a FIRST-CLASS code for incompatible schema/root/contract or --strict-schema migration-required (run_from_env + command_error(3,...) commands.rs:1291-1333, 1242/1269/1312/1327)
deltas.impact: A legitimate version/root incompatibility now exits 3 but Miller misclassifies it as an unexpected crash. The version gate that should fire (IncompatibleExtractException) instead surfaces as a generic JulieExtractException. Interpret must add a case 3 that reads errors[0].code (schema_incompatible/root_mismatch/contract_incompatible) and throws IncompatibleExtractException.

deltas.item: Version gate constants (28/3 -> 1/1) and field location
deltas.old: ExpectedSchemaVersion=28, ExpectedExtractContractVersion=3 (MillerExtractContract.cs:13-14); read from top-level report fields
deltas.new: sqlite_schema_version=1, extract_contract_version=1 (schema.rs:3-4); report_schema_version=1; values live under report.artifact{}
deltas.impact: Miller's pinned constants are off by a wide margin AND look at the wrong nesting level; the gate would reject every new artifact (or silently pass on null). Constants must drop to 1/1 and the cross-check must read report.artifact.sqlite_schema_version / .extract_contract_version / .hash_algorithm.

deltas.item: `--out -` redirects report to stderr
deltas.old: no `export` subcommand exists; Miller always parses the whole stdout as one JSON report (JulieExtractRunner.cs:317)
deltas.new: export is a new subcommand; with `export --out - --json`, JSONL records go to stdout and the JSON report goes to STDERR (write_outcome commands.rs:2006-2020). Other commands keep the report on stdout.
deltas.impact: Not currently invoked by Miller (Miller never runs export), but if Miller adopts JSONL export it must read the report from stderr in that one case. Low risk because Miller's hot path is scan/update/delete/info, all stdout.

deltas.item: `--strict-schema` flag available
deltas.old: no such flag; Miller never opts into strict migration behavior
deltas.new: every read/write command accepts `--strict-schema` which forces exit 3 (SchemaMigrationRequired) instead of silently migrating an older compatible artifact (commands.rs:1307-1318)
deltas.impact: Optional new capability Miller could pass to fail-fast on schema drift rather than relying solely on its own post-exit gate. Not required, but aligns with Miller's fail-loud philosophy.

deltas.item: hash metadata table + value format
deltas.old: Miller reads external_extract_metadata.hash_algorithm=='blake3' and treats files.hash as raw-byte BLAKE3 hex (JulieSchemaGate.cs:48-54, ExtractFileHashReader.cs:17,28)
deltas.new: metadata table is `artifact_metadata` (schema.rs:13-16), hash column is files.content_hash storing the PREFIXED string `blake3:<hex>` (extraction.rs:632); algorithm value is bare `blake3` under artifact_metadata.hash_algorithm
deltas.impact: Crosses into the schema dimension but is reachable from the report's artifact.hash_algorithm too. Miller's freshness BLAKE3 comparison will mismatch because the stored value is `blake3:<hex>`, not bare hex; and the table/key names differ. Flagged here because the report-level gate consumes hash_algorithm.

deltas.item: binary_version format inconsistency (verified upstream bug)
deltas.old: Miller never reads the binary --version at runtime (grep of src for --version returned nothing); gates only on DB/report
deltas.new: report.tool.binary_version is the BARE `0.1.0` (env!(CARGO_PKG_VERSION), commands.rs:1735) but upstream test fixtures assert `julie-extract 0.1.0`; `julie-extract --version` prints `julie-extract 0.1.0`
deltas.impact: Only matters if Miller starts reading tool.binary_version. If it does, it must expect the bare version, not the `julie-extract `-prefixed clap string. Currently inert for Miller.

deltas.item: No timeout / CancellationToken / Kill on spawn (unchanged, but newly riskier)
deltas.old: bare process.WaitForExit() with no timeout/token/kill/WorkingDirectory (JulieExtractRunner.cs:314)
deltas.new: same wrapper code; the new binary's behavior is unchanged here
deltas.impact: Not a delta forced by the migration, but the rewrite touches Run() — the correct-fix opportunity is to add a timeout + Kill while the argv/parse logic is being reworked, since a hung julie-extract blocks bootstrap StartAsync indefinitely with no escape. Flagging so it is not silently skipped during the rewrite.

required_changes.change: Change binaryName from julie-server[.exe] to julie-extract[.exe] (line 61). Remove the leading "extract" token from BuildScanArgs/BuildInfoArgs/BuildUpdateArgs/BuildFileOpArgs (lines 102-103,116,145). Remove the --workspace-id flag pair from BuildScanArgs (line 103). Update all error/help strings that say julie-server. Update Interpret() to add a `case 3` that reads errors[0].code and throws IncompatibleExtractException (lines 162-198). Strongly consider adding a WaitForExit(timeout)+Kill while rewriting Run().

Rewrite the record to the nested Report shape: report_schema_version, status, operation, mode, input{}, artifact{schema_version,extract_contract_version,sqlite_schema_version,hash_algorithm,artifact_id,...}, tool{}, revision{latest_revision_id,created_revision_id}, counts{files_scanned,files_changed,files_unchanged,files_unsupported,files_deleted,files_failed,rows_written{18},totals{18}}, errors[], warnings[]. Rewrite ExtractError -> ReportDiagnostic with {code,message,path,root_relative_path,recoverable,details}. Map old call-sites (FilesTotal/SymbolsTotal/etc.) onto counts.totals.* and counts.rows_written.*.

Read schema/contract/hash from report.artifact.* (not top-level). Update the comparison to the new constants. Treat a null artifact block (e.g. on a path/usage error) as a gate-fail, not a silent pass, since the version fields no longer appear at top level.

Update ExpectedSchemaVersion 28->1, ExpectedExtractContractVersion 3->1 (lines 13-14), and add ExpectedReportSchemaVersion=1. Update PinnedJulieServerVersion semantics (rename to julie-extract; value is product-version 0.1.0 per Cargo.toml, not 7.13.2). Confirm with the human what version string to pin against given the binary_version inconsistency.

Read from artifact_metadata (not external_extract_metadata). Gate sqlite_schema_version/extract_contract_version against the new constants. Account for hash_algorithm value and the files.content_hash `blake3:<hex>` prefix. (Spans into the schema dimension; coordinate.)

Rework DecideBootstrapScan: there is no longer an external_extract_metadata.workspace_id to cross-check against Miller's SHA-256 id (the flag and metadata key are gone). Decide the new rebind/force-scan trigger (e.g. compare artifact.root_path, or rely on root_mismatch exit 3 + force scan).

Update TransientErrorCodes: `flock_timeout` is now `lock_timeout` (reports.rs:263); prefer keying transient classification on the new ReportDiagnostic.recoverable flag rather than a hardcoded code set.
Keep the SHA-256 helper for Miller's own registry, but stop expecting julie to persist/echo it (the --workspace-id flag is gone). Verify no remaining caller assumes julie round-trips the id.

Repoint pins from anortham/julie julie-server 7.13.2 (.tar.gz/.zip release assets) to the julie-extract distribution (different repo, binary name, version, and currently directory-not-archive packaging). This is the packaging dimension but is a hard prerequisite: the CLI layer cannot run a binary that the restore pipeline cannot fetch.

critical_claims: The new binary is named `julie-extract` (Cargo.toml [[bin]] name = "julie-extract"; clap name = "julie-extract" at args.rs:7); there is no `julie-server` binary in julie-extractors.

The six operations (scan/update/delete/info/export/languages) are TOP-LEVEL clap subcommands (args.rs enum Command:16-24, dispatched commands.rs:70-79). There is NO `extract` parent subcommand, so Miller's argv that begins with the literal token "extract" (JulieExtractRunner.cs:103,116,145) would produce a clap usage error (exit 2).

No `--workspace-id` flag exists on any subcommand: ScanArgs (args.rs:26-40), UpdateArgs, DeleteArgs, InfoArgs, ExportArgs, LanguagesArgs contain no such field. Miller currently passes `--workspace-id <id>` on scan (JulieExtractRunner.cs:103).

The new JSON report is a NESTED structure (reports.rs Report:28-41 + custom Serialize:43-66) with report_schema_version, mode, input{}, artifact{}, tool{}, revision{}, counts{rows_written,totals}, warnings[]. schema_version/extract_contract_version/sqlite_schema_version/hash_algorithm live UNDER `artifact` (reports.rs:122-134), not at the top level where Miller's flat ExtractReport (ExtractReport.cs:12-34) reads them.

The new exit-code set is 0/1/2/3, with 3 reserved for incompatible schema/root/contract (run_from_env clap->2 at commands.rs:46-48; command_error(3,...) for SchemaIncompatible/RootMismatch/ContractIncompatible/SchemaMigrationRequired at commands.rs:1291-1333). Miller's Interpret() (JulieExtractRunner.cs:195-197) maps any code other than 0/1/2 to a generic 'unexpected code' crash, so exit 3 is misclassified.

The new product pins sqlite_schema_version=1 and extract_contract_version=1 (schema.rs:3-4), versus Miller's pinned ExpectedSchemaVersion=28 / ExpectedExtractContractVersion=3 (MillerExtractContract.cs:13-14).

With `--json`, the report is emitted as exactly one serde_json line to stdout (write_json commands.rs:2022-2025) for all commands EXCEPT `export --out -`, where the JSON report goes to STDERR (write_outcome commands.rs:2008-2012, ReportStream::Stderr).

The transient-error code Miller hardcodes as `flock_timeout` (IndexerCore) is spelled `lock_timeout` in the new ReportCode enum (reports.rs:263); the new schema also exposes a per-diagnostic `recoverable` bool (reports.rs:305) that Miller does not currently consume.

Miller's spawn has no timeout, no CancellationToken, no Kill, no WorkingDirectory and no env manipulation — confirmed bare process.WaitForExit() at JulieExtractRunner.cs:314 and a ProcessStartInfo (lines 276-283) that sets only FileName/Redirect*/UseShellExecute/CreateNoWindow.

binary_version in the report is the bare `0.1.0` (env!(CARGO_PKG_VERSION) at commands.rs:1735), not the clap `julie-extract 0.1.0` string; Miller does not read it at runtime today (no `--version` usage in src).
open_decisions: What value should Miller pin julie-extract against, given the binary_version inconsistency? The structured report emits bare `0.1.0` while `--version`/fixtures say `julie-extract 0.1.0`. Decide whether to gate on report.artifact.sqlite_schema_version/extract_contract_version (recommended, stable) and ignore binary_version entirely, or to read tool.binary_version (expecting bare form).

How does Miller rebind/detect a stale-root workspace now that `--workspace-id` and external_extract_metadata.workspace_id are gone? Options: (a) compare report.artifact.root_path / artifact_id to a Miller-recorded value, (b) rely on the new exit-3 root_mismatch signal then force a scan. The bootstrap's DecideBootstrapScan logic must be re-specified.

Should Miller adopt `--strict-schema` on scan/update/delete to fail-fast (exit 3) on schema drift instead of relying only on its post-exit-0 cross-check? Aligns with fail-loud philosophy but changes error surfacing.

Should the CLI-layer rewrite also fix the long-standing no-timeout/no-Kill on the spawn (a hung julie-extract blocks bootstrap StartAsync forever)? This is a correctness fix on the path, not a migration requirement — confirm scope.

Does Miller need the new `languages` and `export` subcommands wired (e.g. to drive its own search index from a JSONL stream), or only scan/update/delete/info? The new product explicitly will NOT provide search/embeddings/workspace-registry, so Miller may need to consume `export` JSONL — decide whether the CLI wrapper grows an Export path (which would need the stderr-report special case handled).

Should transient-error classification switch from a hardcoded code set ({data_loss_guard, flock_timeout}) to the new per-diagnostic `recoverable` flag? This is more robust and forward-compatible but changes IndexerCore's contract.

The migration is blocked on packaging: julie-extractors currently publishes a GitHub Actions artifact DIRECTORY (no release assets, no archive, repo slug murphy/julie-extractors). The human must decide the distribution mechanism before the CLI/restore layer can fetch `julie-extract` at all.

diff.dimension: SQLite schema (column-level): old julie-server extract schema (schema_version 28 / extract_contract_version 3 per Miller's pins; the verified-contract doc records the earlier 26/1 generation) vs julie-extractors schema-v1 (sqlite_schema_version 1 / extract_contract_version 1). Table-by-table, column-by-column delta of every table/column/metadata key Miller reads.
diff.old_behavior: Miller reads 11 julie-owned tables from a julie-server `extract` SQLite DB with these exact names/columns (verified in Miller reader source): (1) `symbols` keyed by `id`, with `parent_id`, `metadata` (JSON blob), `file_path`, plus body/span columns start_byte/end_byte/body_start_byte/body_end_byte/body_start_line/body_end_line/start_line/end_line, doc_comment/visibility/code_context/name/signature/kind/language. (2) `identifiers` with `containing_symbol_id`, `target_symbol_id` (read as always-NULL), name/kind/file_path/start_line/start_byte/end_byte. (3) `files` keyed by `path`, with `hash` (raw-byte BLAKE3 hex) and `content`. (4) `relationships` with from_symbol_id/to_symbol_id/kind. (5) `type_arguments` with identifier_id/ordinal/parent_arg_id/type_name/file_path and a bare `id` order-key. (6) `literals` with literal_text/kind/carrier/arg_position/language/containing_symbol_id/start_byte/end_byte/file_path/start_line and `id`. (7) `symbol_annotations` with symbol_id/ordinal/annotation/annotation_key/raw_text/carrier and `id`. (8) `external_extract_metadata` key/value table, keys extract_contract_version, hash_algorithm, workspace_id. (9) `schema_version` table queried SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version),0) FROM schema_version. (10) `canonical_revisions` with revision, workspace_id. (11) `revision_file_changes` with revision, file_path, change_kind, workspace_id. JulieSchemaGate requires the schema_version and external_extract_metadata tables to exist and gates schema=28, extract_contract_version=3, hash_algorithm='blake3'. symbols.metadata JSON carries is_test/test_role. Search/FTS is NOT in the DB; Miller builds its own in-memory BM25.
diff.new_behavior: julie-extractors schema-v1 (verified in crates/julie-extract-artifact/src/schema.rs and metadata.rs) keeps the same logical row domains but RENAMES the metadata/version surface and several key/column names, and DROPS the freshness-by-workspace model and files.content. Confirmed: metadata table is `artifact_metadata(key,value)` NOT external_extract_metadata(key,value,updated_at); there is NO `schema_version` table (schema/contract versions are TEXT rows in artifact_metadata: schema_version, extract_contract_version, sqlite_schema_version, all '1'); symbols PK is `symbol_id` NOT id; symbols parent FK is `parent_symbol_id` NOT parent_id; symbols path column is `path` NOT file_path; the JSON blob column is `metadata_json` NOT metadata on every table; files hash column is `content_hash` NOT hash and stores a PREFIXED 'blake3:<hex>' string NOT bare hex; files `content` TEXT column is DROPPED (files has content_bytes INTEGER); identifiers PK is `identifier_id` NOT id; type_arguments now references `usage_id` (FK to NEW type_argument_usages) and `parent_type_argument_id`, and DROPS identifier_id/file_path from the table; literals/symbol_annotations/relationships PKs become literal_id/annotation_id/relationship_id and none has the bare `id` order-key Miller relies on; `canonical_revisions` is REPLACED by `extraction_revisions(revision_id,...)` with NO workspace_id; `revision_file_changes` is keyed by `revision_id` (INTEGER) with `path` not file_path and NO workspace_id; there is NO workspace_id anywhere (no metadata key, no revision column). The version number collides (old 28 vs new 1) so Miller's exact-match gate rejects it as 'older' regardless. New tables Miller could exploit: type_argument_usages, pending_relationships, type_facts (renamed types), parse_diagnostics, parser_inventory, language_capabilities/_fixtures/_gaps. Still NO FTS/embeddings/search tables (contract test forbids them); Miller keeps owning search and now also owns anything test-detection-related v1 drops.

deltas.item: Metadata table rename: external_extract_metadata -> artifact_metadata
deltas.old: external_extract_metadata(key TEXT PK, value TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)
deltas.new: artifact_metadata(key TEXT PK, value TEXT NOT NULL) - updated_at dropped
deltas.impact: JulieSchemaGate.ReadRequiredMetadataValue, ExtractFileHashReader.ReadHashAlgorithm, ExtractReader.ReadWorkspaceId all SELECT FROM external_extract_metadata. Each throws IncompatibleExtractException / returns null because the table no longer exists. Hard gate fails on the very first read.

deltas.item: Version table dropped: schema_version table no longer exists
deltas.old: SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version),0) FROM schema_version (dedicated table)
deltas.new: No schema_version table; schema_version/sqlite_schema_version/extract_contract_version are TEXT rows inside artifact_metadata
deltas.impact: JulieSchemaGate.ReadSchemaVersion catches 'no such table: schema_version' and throws MissingTable -> IncompatibleExtractException. Gate must read the version from an artifact_metadata key instead.

deltas.item: Schema version number collision: old 28/3 vs new 1/1
deltas.old: MillerExtractContract.ExpectedSchemaVersion=28, ExpectedExtractContractVersion=3
deltas.new: sqlite_schema_version=1, extract_contract_version=1
deltas.impact: Even after fixing the table/key, the pinned constants (28/3) reject schema-v1 as 'older'. Version namespaces are unrelated lineages. MillerExtractContract must be re-pinned to 1/1.

deltas.item: symbols PK rename: id -> symbol_id
deltas.old: SELECT id,... FROM symbols; WHERE id=$id; ORDER BY ..., id
deltas.new: symbols.symbol_id (PK); no column named id
deltas.impact: SqliteSymbolReader bulk SELECT (col 0=id), ExtractReader.ReadDetail/ReadEditSpan (WHERE id=$id), SqliteBridgeReader DbSet query (SELECT id), and all ORDER BY ..., id break with 'no such column: id'. symbol_id is the universal join key so every graph/detail join needs the rename.

deltas.item: symbols parent FK rename: parent_id -> parent_symbol_id
deltas.old: SELECT ..., parent_id FROM symbols (col 8)
deltas.new: symbols.parent_symbol_id
deltas.impact: SqliteSymbolReader reads parent_id at ordinal 8 -> 'no such column'. Containment graph (FindChildren/parent lookup) breaks.

deltas.item: symbols path column rename: file_path -> path
deltas.old: SELECT ..., file_path FROM symbols; WorkspaceIndexFactsReader SELECT DISTINCT file_path FROM symbols; DbSet query SELECT file_path
deltas.new: symbols.path (schema.rs:69); v1 has no symbols.file_path column (only files.path and a denormalized symbols.path)
deltas.impact: SqliteSymbolReader (col 5 file_path), WorkspaceIndexFactsReader.ReadKnownExtensionsCount, and SqliteBridgeReader DbSet/literals/type_args file_path reads break. The symbols/literals/identifiers path column is 'path' in v1.

deltas.item: JSON blob column rename: metadata -> metadata_json (all tables)
deltas.old: SELECT ..., metadata FROM symbols (col 9); ParseTestSignals reads symbols.metadata for is_test/test_role
deltas.new: symbols.metadata_json (and metadata_json on every other table that has it)
deltas.impact: SqliteSymbolReader reads metadata at ordinal 9 -> 'no such column'. Even after rename, is_test/test_role depend on v1 WRITING them - but v1 deliberately drops test_role/test-detection (downstream concern). Test-hiding (search), impact 'likely tests', and trace test seeds silently degrade to (false,null).

deltas.item: files hash rename + value-format change: hash (bare hex) -> content_hash ('blake3:<hex>')
deltas.old: SELECT hash FROM files WHERE path=$path; value is bare BLAKE3 hex
deltas.new: files.content_hash; value is PREFIXED 'blake3:'+hex
deltas.impact: ExtractFileHashReader.ReadFileHash SELECTs files.hash -> 'no such column'. After rename, FreshnessGate compares stored hash to disk BLAKE3 hex; the 'blake3:' prefix makes every comparison mismatch -> every edit flagged stale.

deltas.item: files.content column DROPPED
deltas.old: SELECT content FROM files WHERE path=$path (body slicing + edit freshness baseline)
deltas.new: files has content_bytes INTEGER (a byte count); NO content TEXT column - the artifact does not store file text
deltas.impact: ExtractReader.ReadFileContent/ReadBody/ReadIndexedFileText SELECT files.content -> 'no such column'. inspect(depth=full) body and the edit freshness gate's indexed side lose their source. Miller must read body text from disk or upstream must add a content column. A capability the artifact no longer provides.

deltas.item: identifiers PK rename: id -> identifier_id
deltas.old: identifiers ORDER BY ..., id (references/callees/rename-site queries)
deltas.new: identifiers.identifier_id (PK); no id column
deltas.impact: ExtractReader.ReadReferences/ReadCallees use ORDER BY file_path, start_line, id -> 'no such column: id' (and file_path->path on identifiers too). ReadIdentifierSites ORDER BY file_path, start_byte also hits the path rename.

deltas.item: type_arguments restructured: identifier_id/file_path removed, usage_id/parent_type_argument_id added, bare id gone
deltas.old: SELECT identifier_id, ordinal, parent_arg_id, type_name, file_path FROM type_arguments WHERE identifier_id IS NOT NULL ... ORDER BY identifier_id, ordinal, id
deltas.new: type_arguments(type_argument_id PK, usage_id, parent_type_argument_id, ordinal, type_name) - no identifier_id, no file_path, no metadata_json, no bare id. identifier_id+file_path now live on NEW type_argument_usages(usage_id, identifier_id, file_path, language)
deltas.impact: SqliteBridgeReader.ReadTypeArguments breaks on identifier_id, file_path, parent_arg_id (renamed parent_type_argument_id), and ', id'. Bridge type-argument leg must JOIN type_arguments to type_argument_usages to recover identifier_id/file_path.

deltas.item: literals/symbol_annotations/relationships PK renames + lost bare id order-key
deltas.old: literals/symbol_annotations ORDER BY ..., id; relationships SELECT from_symbol_id,to_symbol_id,kind
deltas.new: literals.literal_id, symbol_annotations.annotation_id, relationships.relationship_id; none has a column named id
deltas.impact: SqliteBridgeReader.ReadLiterals (ORDER BY file_path, start_byte, id) and ReadAnnotations (ORDER BY symbol_id, ordinal, id) break on ', id' (and literals.file_path->path). relationships SELECT itself is unaffected. Payload columns (literal_text, carrier, arg_position, annotation_key, raw_text, from/to_symbol_id, kind) survive with identical names.

deltas.item: Freshness model dropped: canonical_revisions -> extraction_revisions (no workspace_id); revision_file_changes re-keyed to revision_id
deltas.old: SELECT MAX(revision) FROM canonical_revisions WHERE workspace_id=$ws; SELECT revision,file_path,change_kind FROM revision_file_changes WHERE workspace_id=$ws AND revision>$since
deltas.new: extraction_revisions(revision_id PK, parent_revision_id, operation, ...) - NO workspace_id, column is revision_id not revision. revision_file_changes(revision_id, file_id, path, change_kind) - keyed by revision_id, no workspace_id, path not file_path. No canonical_revisions table
deltas.impact: FreshnessReader.LatestRevision and ChangedSince both break: missing table, missing workspace_id column, renamed columns (revision->revision_id, file_path->path). The workspace_id-scoped freshness cursor has no v1 equivalent (one artifact = one root). FreshnessService polling/stale-detection must be redesigned around extraction_revisions.revision_id. change_kind CHECK set is unverified for v1.

deltas.item: workspace_id removed entirely (metadata key + round-trip)
deltas.old: external_extract_metadata key 'workspace_id'; Miller passes --workspace-id (SHA-256 of root) on scan and reads it back to assert binding
deltas.new: No workspace_id metadata key; artifact bound to one canonical root via generated artifact_id + root_path. Caller-supplied artifact-id flag is an explicit OPEN DECISION, not implemented
deltas.impact: ExtractReader.ReadWorkspaceId returns null. IndexBootstrapService persisted-id cross-check (force-rebind on mismatch) loses its signal. Miller's SHA-256 workspace_id is now purely local; it cannot round-trip through the artifact.

diff.dimension: Binary distribution & restore — how Miller acquires the extraction binary, pins its version, and places it where the runtime resolves it
diff.old_behavior: Miller restores a SINGLE pinned binary named `julie-server` (`julie-server.exe` on Windows) from GitHub RELEASE ASSETS of the `anortham/julie` repo. scripts/restore-julie-server.sh + scripts/restore-julie-server.ps1 read scripts/julie-pins.json (version "7.13.2", urlTemplate "https://github.com/anortham/julie/releases/download/v{VER}/{asset}", and 4 per-triple entries each with an asset name + a hand-committed sha256). The script detects the host triple, curl-downloads a versioned ARCHIVE (`julie-v7.13.2-<triple>.tar.gz` for darwin/linux, `.zip` for windows-msvc), verifies sha256 against the pin (julie publishes no checksum assets, so pins are download-verified-and-committed), then extracts ONLY the `julie-server` member from a FLAT multi-binary archive (which also bundles julie-adapter + julie-daemon) via `tar -xzf <archive> -C .tools julie-server`, chmod +x, clears the macOS quarantine xattr, and deletes the archive. A --from-source / MILLER_JULIE_SOURCE path runs `cargo build --manifest-path <root>/Cargo.toml --bin julie-server --release` and copies target/release/julie-server into .tools/; both paths assert `julie-server --version` contains the pinned version " 7.13.2" and abort on mismatch. Build-time: Miller.Server.csproj has a Content item (Conditioned on Exists) that copies repo-root ../../.tools/julie-server to <out>/.tools/julie-server (Link, PreserveNewest), plus an EnsureJulieServerExecutable target that re-chmods +x post Build/Publish on non-Windows. Runtime: WorkspaceContext.ToolsRoot = AppContext.BaseDirectory/.tools; JulieExtractRunner.Locate resolves `julie-server[.exe]` under ToolsRoot first then PATH, else throws FileNotFoundException naming the restore script and v7.13.2. The running .NET code makes NO --version assertion — it gates on the DB report (schema_version 28, extract_contract_version 3, hash_algorithm blake3) via MillerExtractContract (PinnedJulieServerVersion="7.13.2"). Four supported triples: aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc; no linux-arm64 / windows-arm64 (build from source). .tools/ is gitignored.
diff.new_behavior: julie-extractors produces a DIFFERENT binary: `julie-extract` (`julie-extract.exe` on Windows), package/crate `julie-extract-cli`, currently version 2.0.0 (live Cargo.toml line 3; bumped up from the 0.1.0 the MAP recorded — there is a docs/release-notes/v2.0.0.md dated 2026-06-01 alongside the older v0.1.0.md). Built via `cargo build --release -p julie-extract-cli --bin julie-extract`. The binary is fully self-contained (tree-sitter grammars statically compiled in, SQLite bundled via rusqlite `bundled`; macOS binary links only libSystem) — no grammar files or shared libs ship alongside it, so a restore needs only the single binary file. DISTRIBUTION IS NOT YET DOWNLOAD-CONSUMABLE: the `Release Binaries` GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/release-binaries.yml) builds for 3 targets (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc), runs `cargo xtask release package` to STAGE a per-target DIRECTORY (the binary + a `<binary>.sha256` sidecar + 4 contract docs + 3 arch/testing docs + the versioned release note), and uploads it ONLY as a GitHub Actions artifact named `julie-extract-v{version}-{target}` via actions/upload-artifact@v6 (if-no-files-found: error). There is NO GitHub Release, NO attached release asset, NO tarball/zip archive, and NO checksum-of-archive (only a per-binary `.sha256` sidecar, format `{hex}  dist/{target}/julie-extract{exe_suffix}`). There are currently NO git tags in the repo, so the `v*`-tag trigger has never fired; the release path is local-staging / manual-promotion only. The workspace repository slug is `github.com/murphy/julie-extractors` (a placeholder; not anortham). Version metadata: clap `--version` prints `julie-extract <CARGO_PKG_VERSION>` (a fresh 2.0.0 build prints `julie-extract 2.0.0`; the stale on-disk build prints `julie-extract 0.1.0`); structured `tool.binary_version` and artifact_metadata.binary_version are the BARE `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` (no `julie-extract ` prefix). The artifact's own version surface is sqlite_schema_version=1 / extract_contract_version=1 / hash_algorithm "blake3" stored in `artifact_metadata` (NOT `external_extract_metadata`); content hash is `files.content_hash` holding a `blake3:<hex>` PREFIXED string. Triple coverage drops x86_64-apple-darwin (Intel Mac) relative to Miller's expected set.

Decide whether the distribution swap lands as one atomic migration with the schema-reader rewrite, or whether a transitional dual-support window is needed.

diff.old_behavior:
Miller's freshness/incremental/metadata model is built against julie-server v7.13.2 / schema 28 / extract_contract_version 3, gated on external_extract_metadata.hash_algorithm='blake3'. Three independent freshness mechanisms exist, each tightly coupled to specific julie columns:

(1) Index-rebuild freshness (FreshnessReader + a 2s poll): reads `SELECT MAX(revision) FROM canonical_revisions WHERE workspace_id=$ws` as a per-workspace cursor (FreshnessReader.cs:74-76). When MAX(revision) > the held index's BuiltRevision, Miller does a FULL in-memory reload (not incremental). The changed-file delta `SELECT revision, file_path, change_kind FROM revision_file_changes WHERE workspace_id=$ws AND revision>$since` (FreshnessReader.cs:96-99) is read but explicitly NOT wired to an incremental patch ("Used by the future incremental rebuild (decision-5)"). change_kind is hard-parsed to exactly {added, modified, deleted}; any other value THROWS InvalidOperationException as schema drift (FreshnessReader.cs:118-126).

(2) Per-file edit gate (FreshnessGate): reads `files.hash` (raw-byte BLAKE3 hex), reads external_extract_metadata.hash_algorithm and requires it == 'blake3' (FreshnessGate.cs:62-63), hashes disk bytes with Blake3FileHex producing BARE lowercase hex (ContentHasher.cs:16, Convert.ToHexStringLower), and compares via StalenessCheck.Check using string.Equals(...Ordinal) (StalenessCheck.cs:78). A bare-hex vs bare-hex ordinal compare.

(3) Incremental re-extract: Miller drives julie with `scan` (force=false hash-delta reconcile, force=true full rebuild), plus per-file `update --file`/`delete --file`, routed by a leader-elected FileSystemWatcher (full scan only on watcher overflow/HEAD move). scan carries `--workspace-id <SHA256-hex-of-canonical-root>`; update/delete do not. Miller reads julie's persisted external_extract_metadata.workspace_id and asserts equality, force-rebinding on mismatch (DecideBootstrapScan: missing DB→delta scan; mismatched workspace_id→force scan). ExtractReport carries flat freshness fields workspace_id/revision (long)/files_updated/files_deleted/hash_algorithm. update is hash-no-op on unchanged content; delete is idempotent (status=not_found, exit 0).

Metadata reads: external_extract_metadata (key/value) for hash_algorithm + extract_contract_version + workspace_id; symbols.metadata JSON for is_test/test_role.
diff.new_behavior:
julie-extract 0.1.0 / sqlite_schema_version 1 / extract_contract_version 1, with hash recorded as artifact_metadata.hash_algorithm='blake3'. The freshness/incremental/metadata surface changed shape in every dimension Miller couples to:

(1) Revision tables: `canonical_revisions` is GONE; replaced by `extraction_revisions` keyed by `revision_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (no `revision` column, no `workspace_id` column at all — schema.rs:28-40). `revision_file_changes` keeps the name but its columns are (revision_id, file_id, path, change_kind) — NO `workspace_id` (schema.rs:43-49). One artifact is bound to one canonical root with a generated artifact_id, so there is no workspace_id to filter by. change_kind enum values are now {inserted, updated, deleted, unsupported} (model.rs:53-66), NOT {added, modified, deleted}.

(2) File hash: column renamed `files.hash` → `files.content_hash` and the stored VALUE is now PREFIXED: `blake3:<64-hex>` (extraction.rs:632 format!("blake3:{}", ...)). The algorithm label lives at artifact_metadata.hash_algorithm (table renamed external_extract_metadata → artifact_metadata).

(3) Incremental re-extract: same conceptual model survives — `scan` (incremental) skips unchanged files via content_hash comparison when mode != Force (writer.rs:246-255 skip_unchanged_content), `scan --force` rebuilds, `update --file`/`delete --file` are per-file, `info` is read-only preflight. delete hard-removes file rows (delete_file_rows) and records a Deleted change; missing rows → not_found exit 0 (matches old idempotency). update on unsupported/ignored → status=unsupported, deletes stale rows, exit 0.

(4) Report shape: NESTED, not flat. revision is an object {latest_revision_id, created_revision_id} (reports.md:44-47), counts is an object with counts.rows_written + counts.totals maps keyed by table name (reports.md:48-95), artifact metadata is a nested {artifact_id, schema_version, extract_contract_version, sqlite_schema_version, hash_algorithm,...} object. No flat `revision`/`files_total`/`workspace_id`/`files_updated`/`files_deleted` top-level fields. Commands with no artifact (languages) set revision=null.

(5) Metadata: artifact_metadata(key,value) with 11 required keys (no workspace_id key — uses artifact_id + root_path). symbols.metadata → symbols.metadata_json; is_test/test_role are deliberately NOT artifact fields (test detection is a downstream concern, omitted from v1).

deltas.item: Revision cursor table renamed and re-keyed: canonical_revisions(revision, workspace_id) → extraction_revisions(revision_id, ...) with NO workspace_id
deltas.old: SELECT MAX(revision) FROM canonical_revisions WHERE workspace_id = $ws
deltas.new: SELECT MAX(revision_id) FROM extraction_revisions  (no workspace_id column; one artifact = one root)
deltas.impact: FreshnessReader.LatestRevision query fails (table/column do not exist) → the 2s poll-driven index-rebuild freshness loop is fully broken. The WHERE workspace_id clause has no target column.

deltas.item: revision_file_changes lost workspace_id and changed change_kind vocabulary
deltas.old: SELECT revision, file_path, change_kind FROM revision_file_changes WHERE workspace_id=$ws AND revision>$since; change_kind ∈ {added,modified,deleted}
deltas.new: columns are (revision_id, file_id, path, change_kind); no workspace_id, no `revision` col, path not file_path; change_kind ∈ {inserted,updated,deleted,unsupported}
deltas.impact: ChangedSince query fails (workspace_id/revision/file_path columns gone). Even if columns are remapped, ParseChangeKind THROWS InvalidOperationException on 'inserted','updated','unsupported' — three of four new values are unrecognized, so the parser hard-fails on any non-deleted change.

deltas.item: File hash column renamed and value format prefixed
deltas.old: files.hash = bare lowercase BLAKE3 hex (e.g. 'a1b2...'); Miller compares with bare Convert.ToHexStringLower(blake3)
deltas.new: files.content_hash = 'blake3:<64-hex>' (literal 'blake3:' prefix, extraction.rs:632)
deltas.impact: ExtractFileHashReader.ReadFileHash 'SELECT hash FROM files' fails (no `hash` column). Even after renaming to content_hash, StalenessCheck.Check does string.Equals(indexedHash, currentHash, Ordinal) where currentHash is bare hex and indexedHash carries the 'blake3:' prefix → ALWAYS unequal → every file reads Stale → edit tool blocks every edit (unless allow_stale). Must strip the 'blake3:' prefix before comparison.

deltas.item: Metadata table renamed external_extract_metadata → artifact_metadata; hash_algorithm key relocates
deltas.old: SELECT value FROM external_extract_metadata WHERE key='hash_algorithm' (and key='extract_contract_version', key='workspace_id')
deltas.new: SELECT value FROM artifact_metadata WHERE key='hash_algorithm' (keys: artifact_id, root_path, schema_version, extract_contract_version, sqlite_schema_version, binary_version, hash_algorithm, parser_inventory_fingerprint, capability_snapshot_fingerprint, created_at, updated_at — NO workspace_id key)
deltas.impact: ExtractFileHashReader.ReadHashAlgorithm, JulieSchemaGate gate reads, and ExtractReader workspace_id read all target a nonexistent table. The hash_algorithm gate (FreshnessGate.cs:63) returns null → IndexedContentFound=false → all edits blocked. workspace_id key does not exist; Miller's persisted-id cross-check (DecideBootstrapScan force-rebind) has nothing to read.

deltas.item: workspace_id is no longer a julie concept; scan --workspace-id flag and persisted-id rebind disappear
deltas.old: scan argv passes --workspace-id <SHA256 of canonical root>; julie persists it; Miller asserts external_extract_metadata.workspace_id == stable id, force-scans on mismatch (DecideBootstrapScan)
deltas.new: julie-extract scan has NO --workspace-id flag; artifact_id is generated internally ('artifact-<nanos>'); root binding is via artifact_metadata.root_path and a root_mismatch typed error (exit 3) unless scan --force

Miller's SHA-256(canonical-root) workspace_id is now purely a MILLER-internal registry key (~/.miller/workspaces.db), no longer echoed by/asserted against julie. Bootstrap force-rebind logic must switch from workspace_id-mismatch detection to artifact_metadata.root_path comparison (or rely on julie's exit-3 root_mismatch).

deltas.item: ExtractReport JSON shape: flat freshness fields → nested objects
deltas.old: flat: revision (long), workspace_id, files_updated, files_deleted, hash_algorithm, files_total/symbols_total/...; serde db→db_path
deltas.new: nested: revision={latest_revision_id, created_revision_id}; counts={files_scanned,files_changed,files_unchanged,files_unsupported,files_deleted,files_failed, rows_written{...}, totals{...}}; artifact={artifact_id,schema_version,...,hash_algorithm}; tool={binary_name,binary_version}; report_schema_version=1; revision=null for languages

Miller's freshness-from-report and ExtractVersionMismatch.VerifyReport (reads report.SchemaVersion/ExtractContractVersion/HashAlgorithm at the top level) silently see null and skip the cross-check, OR the snake_case revision-object collides with the long? Revision field. The whole report parse layer needs a new nested model.

deltas.old: schema_version=28, extract_contract_version=3, PinnedJulieServerVersion='7.13.2'
deltas.new: sqlite_schema_version=1, extract_contract_version=1, binary julie-extract 0.1.0 (schema_version key also '1')

deltas.item: Incremental hash-delta scan + per-file update/delete model SURVIVES (this is the compatible part)
deltas.old: scan(force=false) = hash-delta reconcile skipping unchanged; scan --force = full rebuild; update --file = hash-gated upsert; delete --file = idempotent row removal (not_found exit 0)
deltas.new: scan(incremental) skips files where existing.content_hash == new content_hash unless mode=Force (writer.rs:246-255); scan --force rebuilds; update --file single_file; delete --file hard-removes rows (delete_file_rows), missing→not_found exit 0; update on unsupported→status unsupported, removes stale rows, exit 0

deltas.item: OPPORTUNITY: revision_file_changes delta is now richer (inserted/updated/deleted/unsupported) and could finally drive an INCREMENTAL in-memory rebuild instead of full reload
deltas.old: revision_file_changes delta is read by FreshnessReader.ChangedSince but NOT wired to rebuild; freshness triggers a FULL RepositoryIndexLoader.Load reload

Avoids full O(repo) reload on every edit. Requires teaching the delta model the new 4-value change_kind and the file_id↔path mapping.

deltas.item: Freshness cursor cross-instance semantics: revision_id is artifact-global, not workspace-scoped
deltas.old: MAX(revision) per workspace_id; multiple workspaces could share one DB (in principle) and each had an independent cursor
deltas.new: revision_id is a single monotonic PK over the whole artifact (one root per artifact); created_revision_id is the revision a mutation created, latest_revision_id is the artifact head

deltas.item: Binary name and version-detection change (affects freshness preflight via info)

deltas.new: binary 'julie-extract'; report.tool.binary_version is BARE '0.1.0'; info is the canonical version-gating preflight (artifact.* nested metadata); CLI --version prints 'julie-extract 0.1.0'

Miller's ContentHasher.Blake3FileHex produces BARE hex (ContentHasher.cs:16) and StalenessCheck compares with string.Equals(...Ordinal) (StalenessCheck.cs:78), so every file would read Stale and every edit would block unless the prefix is stripped.

diff.dimension: Capability ownership — what Miller must now build itself (NON-GOALS of julie-extract: search index, embeddings, workspace registry, watcher, analysis/test-quality/reference-scores)
diff.old_behavior: Under the OLD julie-server `extract` contract (schema 28 / extract_contract_version 3 / hash_algorithm=blake3, binary `julie-server`), julie-server's job was ALREADY scoped to raw extraction only. Verified positively against Miller source: Miller does NOT receive a search index, embeddings, a workspace registry, a watcher, or reference-scores from julie-server, and never did. (1) SEARCH: Miller builds its OWN in-memory BM25 inverted index (src/Miller.Core/Search/MillerSearchIndex.cs, K1=1.2/B=0.75/ExactNameBoost=1.5) from raw `symbols.name`+`symbols.signature`; grep of src/**/*.cs for fts5|fts4|porter|unicode61|trigram|virtual table|bm25(|MATCH returned ZERO SQLite FTS usages (only C# string/regex "Match" and comments). julie's own *_fts tables were dropped in migration 007 long ago — they never crossed the extract boundary. (2) EMBEDDINGS: zero embedding/vec0/sqlite-vec usage in Miller src; the only "embedding" hits are comments stating embeddings are GONE (Posting.cs:8 "now that embeddings are gone") and TraceTool.cs:18 "no DB, no embeddings". (3) WORKSPACE REGISTRY: Miller already OWNS it — the only two CREATE TABLE statements in all of src are `workspaces` (WorkspaceRegistry.cs:9, in ~/.miller/workspaces.db) and `tool_telemetry` (TelemetryLedger.cs:19); neither is a julie table. (4) WATCHER: Miller already OWNS it — IndexerService.cs has its own leader-elected System.IO.FileSystemWatcher (lines 41-42, 377, 398) plus a git-HEAD watcher; julie-server never provided a long-running watcher, only one-shot update/delete/scan ops driven BY Miller's watcher. (5) ANALYSIS / REFERENCE-SCORES: Miller does NOT read `reference_score` anywhere (grep found only `analysis_state` parsed as a report field in ExtractReport.cs:20, never consumed for ranking), and never invokes an `analyze` pass. The ONE analysis-adjacent signal Miller DOES consume from julie is per-symbol TEST DETECTION: SqliteSymbolReader.ParseTestSignals reads `symbols.metadata` JSON for keys `is_test` (bool) and `test_role` (string), feeding test-aware behavior in search (hide tests), impact ("which tests to run" partition via IndexedSymbol.IsTest), and trace/bridge. Test detection is julie's cross-language test_detection.rs output, delivered inside the `metadata` JSON blob column under schema 28.
diff.new_behavior: Under the NEW `julie-extract` v1 product (binary `julie-extract` 0.1.0 / sqlite_schema_version=1 / extract_contract_version=1, repo murphy/julie-extractors), the product boundary is EXPLICITLY scoped to raw extraction and the five NON-GOALS are formal exclusions enforced by a contract test (schema_contract.rs:40-53 asserts search_index, embeddings, workspace_registry, mcp_tools, watcher_state, reference_scores, test_quality tables are ABSENT). So for SEARCH, EMBEDDINGS, WORKSPACE REGISTRY, WATCHER, and REFERENCE-SCORES the migration is MECHANICAL / ZERO-RISK: julie-server never supplied any of them and Miller already owns the ones it has (BM25 index, ~/.miller/workspaces.db registry, FileSystemWatcher). Miller builds NO new subsystem for these four-and-a-half capabilities. The migration is therefore NOT a "Miller must build new subsystems" exercise for the named non-goals — it is a CLI+schema rename/reshape exercise. HOWEVER, the ONE capability Miller does depend on — cross-language TEST DETECTION — survives in v1 but in a DIFFERENT SHAPE, and this is the load-bearing delta for this dimension. Verified against live julie-extractors source: v1 PROMOTED test detection to TYPED COLUMNS on `symbols`: `is_test INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `test_container INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `test_lifecycle INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` (schema.rs:93-95), with index `idx_symbols_is_test` (schema.rs:296); extraction.rs:224-226 reads is_test/test_container/test_lifecycle flags from the upstream symbol metadata and writes the typed columns. CRITICALLY: there is NO `test_role` column in v1 (grep test_role in schema.rs = 0 matches) — the role string is gone, replaced by two finer boolean flags (test_container, test_lifecycle). This directly CONTRADICTS the MAP's v1-schema reader and migration-story reader, which both asserted is_test/test_role were deliberately EXCLUDED from v1; the live schema shows is_test PRESENT (promoted), test_role DROPPED. Miller's reader (SqliteSymbolReader.ParseTestSignals) substring-probes a `metadata` JSON column for "is_test"/"test_role" — under v1 the column is named `metadata_json`, is_test is a sibling typed column (not in JSON), and test_role does not exist. So Miller's test-aware features (search hide-tests, impact test-partition, trace seeds) SILENTLY DEGRADE to (false, null) for every symbol unless the reader is rewritten to read the typed `symbols.is_test` column.

deltas.item: Embeddings ownership
deltas.old: Miller uses NO embeddings (positively verified: only comments noting embeddings are 'gone'); julie-server's extract never delivered vectors to Miller.
deltas.new: julie-extract v1 forbids any embeddings/vec0 table (schema_contract.rs:42).
deltas.impact: ZERO migration work. Not a capability Miller consumes.

deltas.item: Workspace registry ownership
deltas.old: Miller already OWNS the registry: ~/.miller/workspaces.db with a Miller-created `workspaces` table (WorkspaceRegistry.cs:9). julie-server's extract DB is per-root and carries only external_extract_metadata.workspace_id (a scoping value Miller computes itself as SHA-256 of canonical root).
deltas.new: julie-extract v1 forbids any workspace_registry table (schema_contract.rs:43); artifact is bound to ONE canonical root with a generated artifact_id; no workspace_id field (reports.md avoids old workspace_id name).
deltas.impact: ZERO new-subsystem work — Miller owns the registry. BUT a small mechanical delta: v1 metadata no longer carries `workspace_id` (Miller reads external_extract_metadata.workspace_id at ExtractReader.cs:240 today). Miller already computes its own stable workspace_id via SHA-256(canonical root) (WorkspaceId.cs), so it can drop the read; the IndexBootstrapService persisted-id cross-check (force-rebind on mismatch) loses its julie-echoed counterpart and must rely solely on Miller's own id.

deltas.item: Watcher ownership
deltas.old: Miller already OWNS a leader-elected FileSystemWatcher (IndexerService.cs:41-42,377,398) + git-HEAD watcher; it drives julie-server's one-shot update/delete/scan ops on a ~1s debounce. julie-server never ran a long-running watcher.
deltas.new: julie-extract v1 forbids any watcher_state table and the product explicitly will NOT own a long-running watcher (vision.md non-goal); update/delete remain per-event CLI commands a watcher integration drives externally.
deltas.impact: ZERO new-subsystem work. Miller's watcher is unchanged. The watcher still calls the CLI per-event — only the argv changes (see CLI-invocation delta in the CLI dimension).

deltas.item: Reference-scores / analysis ownership
deltas.old: Miller does NOT read reference_score from julie at all (grep: only analysis_state parsed-but-unused in ExtractReport.cs:20; no analyze invocation). Search ranking (BM25) and bridge confidence are computed in Miller.Core. So Miller never depended on julie's --analyze reference-scoring.
deltas.new: julie-extract v1 forbids reference_scores AND test_quality tables (schema_contract.rs:46-47); analysis/reference-scoring/test-quality are declared downstream concerns; there is NO analyze command (the v1 CLI has scan/update/delete/info/export/languages only).
deltas.impact: ZERO migration work for reference-scores — Miller never consumed them. The unused `analysis_state` field in ExtractReport can be dropped. Miller's name-based edge over-approximation (identifiers.target_symbol_id always NULL) is unchanged: v1 still leaves target_symbol_id resolution to the consumer, no analyze pass to wait on.

deltas.item: Cross-language TEST DETECTION (the one analysis-adjacent capability Miller DOES consume) — column shape change
deltas.old: julie-server delivers test detection inside the `symbols.metadata` JSON blob: keys is_test (bool, emitted only when true) and test_role (string: unit/integration/e2e). Miller's SqliteSymbolReader.ParseTestSignals substring-probes `metadata` for "is_test"/"test_role" then JSON-parses both. Feeds search hide-tests (SearchTool.cs:136), impact test-partition (ImpactTool.cs:186), trace/bridge test seeds.
deltas.new: julie-extract v1 PROMOTED test detection to TYPED COLUMNS on symbols: is_test INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, test_container INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, test_lifecycle INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (schema.rs:93-95) + idx_symbols_is_test (schema.rs:296). The JSON blob column is renamed `metadata` -> `metadata_json`. There is NO test_role column (dropped); the role string is replaced by two finer booleans (test_container / test_lifecycle).
deltas.impact: HIGH — this is the load-bearing capability-ownership delta. Miller MUST rewrite SqliteSymbolReader to (a) SELECT the typed `is_test` column instead of probing the JSON blob, (b) rename the JSON column read to `metadata_json`, and (c) decide what to do about the LOST test_role: TestRole is a Miller.Core contract type used by ImpactTool, RouteBridge, BridgeGraphBuilder — v1 has no role string, so either derive a coarse role from test_container/test_lifecycle or drop TestRole. If unfixed, ParseTestSignals returns (false,null) for EVERY symbol (the substring pre-filter never matches the renamed column), SILENTLY disabling all test-aware behavior with no error.

deltas.item: Metadata TABLE rename (gate surface) — adjacent to all ownership reads
deltas.old: Miller's compatibility gate (JulieSchemaGate) requires `external_extract_metadata` (key/value) and `schema_version` (version) tables; reads keys extract_contract_version, hash_algorithm, workspace_id. Pinned schema=28, contract=3.
deltas.new: julie-extract v1 names the metadata table `artifact_metadata` (schema.rs:13); the schema/contract version lives in artifact_metadata keys sqlite_schema_version=1 / extract_contract_version=1 (no separate schema_version table); required keys include artifact_id, root_path, hash_algorithm, parser_inventory_fingerprint, etc.
deltas.impact: MED — not a NEW subsystem, but every Miller capability that reads metadata (gate, freshness hash_algorithm check, workspace_id scoping) must retarget the table name and version pins. This is the table-rename plumbing that the test-detection delta rides on.

deltas.item: File-freshness hash (underpins the watcher-driven incremental capability)
deltas.old: Miller reads `files.hash` as a BARE blake3 hex and guards on external_extract_metadata.hash_algorithm='blake3' (ExtractFileHashReader.cs:17,28). FreshnessGate BLAKE3-hashes disk bytes and compares to files.hash.
deltas.new: julie-extract v1 stores `files.content_hash` (renamed) as a PREFIXED string 'blake3:<hex>' (extraction.rs content_hash_bytes), with artifact_metadata.hash_algorithm='blake3'.
deltas.impact: MED — the freshness/incremental capability is Miller-owned and stays, but the hash COLUMN renamed (hash -> content_hash) AND the VALUE format gained a 'blake3:' prefix. Miller's edit freshness gate compares raw blake3 hex; against v1 it must strip the 'blake3:' prefix or every freshness verdict is wrong (always-stale). Not a non-goal subsystem, but a silent-corruption hazard on the path.

required_changes.change: Rewrite test-signal read: SELECT the typed `is_test` column from v1 symbols (not a JSON probe); rename the JSON blob column from `metadata` to `metadata_json`; handle the LOSS of `test_role` (no such column in v1) by either reading test_container/test_lifecycle and deriving a coarse role, or removing TestRole from the projection. Without this, all test-aware behavior silently degrades to non-test for every symbol.

Decide the fate of the TestRole contract type: v1 dropped the role string and replaced it with test_container/test_lifecycle booleans. Either map the two booleans onto a coarse role or delete TestRole and its consumers (SymbolDetail, ImpactTool, RouteBridge, BridgeGraphBuilder reference it).

Retarget the compatibility gate from `external_extract_metadata`/`schema_version` to v1's `artifact_metadata` table and its sqlite_schema_version/extract_contract_version keys; this is the surface every metadata-backed capability (freshness, workspace_id scoping) reads through.

Repin the version constants: ExpectedSchemaVersion 28 -> 1 (sqlite_schema_version), ExpectedExtractContractVersion 3 -> 1, PinnedJulieServerVersion 7.13.2 -> julie-extract 0.1.0 (and rename the binary). Note v1 version numbers are LOWER than the old pins — the gate's 'reject older' logic must not treat v1 as a downgrade.

Rename the freshness hash column read from `files.hash` to `files.content_hash` and strip the 'blake3:' prefix from the stored value before comparing to Miller's raw blake3 disk hash. Retarget the hash_algorithm key read from external_extract_metadata to artifact_metadata.
Account for the 'blake3:'-prefixed content_hash so the edit freshness gate does not report every file stale.
Drop or retarget the workspace_id read (v1 has no workspace_id metadata key — artifact is root-bound with a generated artifact_id); Miller already computes its own workspace_id via SHA-256.

Rework the persisted-workspace-id cross-check: v1 does not echo Miller's workspace_id into metadata, so the force-rebind-on-mismatch logic must rely on Miller's own stable id (or on artifact_id/root_path) instead of a julie-echoed value.
Remove the unused analysis_state field and align report parsing to v1's report schema (report_schema_version=1, status enum, counts) — the old analyze/reference-score-adjacent fields are gone.

# Miller → julie-extractors Migration: Comparative Analyst's Brief

**Scope:** Migrating Miller (`/Users/murphy/source/miller`) off the pinned `julie-server extract` (schema 28 / contract 3) onto julie-extractors' new `julie-extract` binary (schema 1 / contract 1).
**Status of inputs:** The MAP/DIFF were partially refuted by the live-source verification pass. This brief applies those corrections. Verdicts cited inline.

---

## 1. Executive delta

- **Not mechanical. This is a contract-epoch rewrite of Miller's entire julie-facing seam.** Every read path (subprocess argv, exit-code map, JSON report parser, SQLite reader, freshness gate, schema gate, restore pipeline) breaks at once. It is renames + reshapes, not new algorithms — but the surface is wide and the failures are interlocking.
- **Miller does NOT need to build new subsystems for the five "non-goals."** Verified positively: Miller already owns its BM25 search (`MillerSearchIndex.cs`), already has no embeddings, already owns its workspace registry (`workspaces` table) and watcher (`IndexerService.FileSystemWatcher`), and never consumed reference-scores. julie-extract dropping all five costs Miller zero new-subsystem work. (Verdicts: all 5 **confirmed**.)
- **The single biggest risk is the SQLite read layer.** ~7 reader files address tables/columns by old names AND by positional ordinal. Against schema-v1 they fail loudly (missing-table/missing-column), not silently — `JulieSchemaGate.Verify` throws `IncompatibleExtractException` first (no `schema_version` table; 28≠1). That loud failure is actually good: no silent data corruption.
- **The freshness model is the deepest structural change.** `canonical_revisions` (workspace_id-scoped cursor) is gone; replaced by `extraction_revisions(revision_id)` with no workspace_id and no `revision` column. `revision_file_changes` loses workspace_id, renames `revision→revision_id`/`file_path→path`, and changes `change_kind` from `{added,modified,deleted}` to `{inserted,updated,deleted,unsupported}` — Miller's `ParseChangeKind` throws on 3 of the 4 new values.
- **Test detection SURVIVES and is RICHER, not dropped.** The MAP/DIFF claim "test_role dropped, is_test excluded" is **refuted**. v1 promotes `is_test`/`test_container`/`test_lifecycle` to typed indexed columns AND keeps them in `metadata_json` (verified: `json_extract(metadata_json,'$.is_test')` contract test). `test_role` never existed in v1 — it was decomposed into the two booleans. Miller's `TestRole` contract type needs a decision (derive from the booleans or drop it), but test-awareness is an upgrade opportunity, not a loss.
- **There is no acquisition path today.** **BLOCKER.** julie-extractors publishes no GitHub Release, no archive, no checksummed downloadable asset — only a per-target Actions-artifact directory, no git tags, repo slug is a placeholder (`murphy/julie-extractors` vs real `anortham`). Miller's download-based restore has nothing to point at. From-source build is the only available path until upstream publishes.
- **Two silent-corruption traps if the loud gate were bypassed:** (a) `files.content_hash` is `blake3:<hex>` prefixed vs Miller's bare-hex compare → every file reads stale; (b) `metadata_json` column rename → test signals silently go `(false,null)`. Both are downstream of the schema gate, so they only bite after the gate is fixed.
- **The version-number collision is real but the fix is one line.** Old 28/3 → new 1/1; the exact-match gate rejects v1 as "older" once table wiring is correct. Re-pin `MillerExtractContract`.

---

Binary: `julie-server` → `julie-extract` (verified **confirmed**: `Cargo.toml [[bin]] name="julie-extract"`, `args.rs:7`). No `extract` parent subcommand; the six ops are top-level clap subcommands. Empirically verified: passing `extract` first yields `error: unrecognized subcommand 'extract'` exit 2.

| Scan | `extract --db D --root R --workspace-id ID --json scan [--force]` (`:102-106`) | `scan --root R --db D [--force] [--ignore-file…] [--strict-schema] [--json]` | drop `extract` token; **drop `--workspace-id` (flag does not exist; forbidden token)** |

Note: `file_outside_root`/`invalid_path`/`file_not_found` are exit **1**, not 3 — consumers must key off `errors[].code`, not the exit code alone.

Special case: `export --out -` puts the report on **stderr** (verified **confirmed**); inert for Miller unless it adopts export.

**Transient-error code:** Miller hardcodes `flock_timeout`; new enum spells it `lock_timeout` (verified **confirmed**, `reports.rs:263`). New per-diagnostic `recoverable: bool` exists (`reports.rs:305`) and Miller does not consume it (verified **confirmed**) — prefer it over a hardcoded code set.

**No timeout/Kill on spawn** (verified **confirmed**, bare `WaitForExit()` `:314`): unchanged by the migration, but the rewrite touches `Run()` — the correct-fix opportunity is to add a timeout + Kill so a hung `julie-extract` can't block bootstrap `StartAsync` forever. 1. **Acquisition: wait for release assets, or build from source?** julie-extractors publishes nothing downloadable today (no Release, no archive, no tag, placeholder repo slug). Either (a) block the migration until upstream ships checksummed assets under a real slug, or (b) make Miller's restore from-source-only (`-p julie-extract-cli --bin julie-extract`) against a julie-extractors checkout in the interim. The download branch of the restore scripts cannot be written meaningfully until this is settled.

2. **What version to pin, and what field to gate on?** Live crate is 2.0.0 but the structured `tool.binary_version` is bare (no `julie-extract ` prefix), the on-disk binary still reports 0.1.0, and fixtures assert `julie-extract 0.1.0`. Recommend gating on `report.artifact.sqlite_schema_version`/`extract_contract_version` (stable) and ignoring `binary_version` entirely. Confirm.

3. **`files.content` is gone — re-source body text from disk, or request a content column upstream?** Disk text ≠ indexed snapshot, which changes the edit-freshness contract (the gate currently compares against julie's stored snapshot). This affects `inspect(full)` body slicing AND every edit op. Big enough to surface explicitly.

4. **Workspace identity / rebind model.** No `--workspace-id` flag and no `workspace_id` metadata key in v1; artifact is root-bound with a generated `artifact-<nanos>` id. Options: compare `artifact_metadata.root_path`, rely on exit-3 `root_mismatch` + force scan, or request a caller-supplied `--artifact-id` flag (an explicit upstream open decision — Miller is the named likely caller).

5. **`TestRole` fate.** v1 replaced the role string with `test_container`/`test_lifecycle` booleans (richer). Derive a coarse role for backward compat, or drop `TestRole` and migrate `ImpactTool`/`RouteBridge`/`BridgeGraphBuilder` to the booleans (cleaner, more files touched).

6. **`change_kind` "unsupported" semantics.** New value with no old equivalent (file exists but unparseable). Treat as delete-from-index, no-op, or distinct state?

7. **Seize the incremental-rebuild opportunity now?** v1's richer 4-value `change_kind` delta makes the long-deferred in-memory incremental patch (vs full `RepositoryIndexLoader.Load` reload) viable. Adds `file_id↔path` mapping complexity. In or out of this migration's scope?

8. **Adopt `--strict-schema` and/or `export` JSONL?** `--strict-schema` fails-fast (exit 3) on drift, aligning with Miller's fail-loud philosophy. `export` is the only julie path that would feed an external JSONL pipeline — not needed for parity, but relevant if Miller ever wants a streamed feed (would require handling the stderr-report special case).

9. **Sequencing.** The binary re-pin, schema-gate change (28/3→1/1), table/column renames, freshness rewrite, and bootstrap rework are interlocking. Land as one atomic migration, or behind a feature flag against a from-source build first?
